iterations.theme: Hormoni kao izgovor ili saveznik: kortizol, inzulin, prehrambene navike, stres i plodnost

sections.subtitle: Iz Dubrovnika u Mostar preko Zagrebačke ulice: razgovor o ženskom zdravlju počinje šalom
sections.screenshot_description: Ana Pavlović u studiju kroz smijeh pita Mirnu Sentić zašto se planirala voziti šest sati
sections.content:
Nova epizoda podcasta **„Rastući s djecom“** počinje nizom isječaka koji odmah otkrivaju ton razgovora. Spominju se kave koje „boostaju“ kortizol, ovulacija koju koči stres i misao da roditeljstvo ne počinje plusom na testu, nego idejom da dvoje ljudi postanu roditelji.

Voditeljica **Ana Pavlović** zatim najavljuje da je epizoda posvećena ženama i ženskom zdravlju. Napominje da je ovo i prilika za muškarce koji žele bolje razumjeti kako hormoni djeluju na žene. Naglašava da središnje pitanje nije samo kako hormoni djeluju na nas, nego i kako mi možemo djelovati na njih. Upravo zato gošća nije endokrinologinja, nego nutricionistica **Mirna Sentić**.

Razgovor je krenuo tek nakon tehničkih poteškoća i „brojnih peripetija“ oko samog dogovora. Ana se ne propušta našaliti na račun gošće. Mirna je, naime, iz Dubrovnika planirala putovati čak šest sati do Mostara. Objašnjenje je simpatično: studio se nalazi u **Zagrebačkoj ulici**, a relacija Dubrovnik–Zagreb traje upravo šest sati. „To su moji hormoni“, odgovara Mirna kroz smijeh.

Dodaje da je njezina logika bila jednostavna: kad su u pitanju dobri gosti, „sve se događa u Velegradu“, pa mora biti Zagreb. Ne slaže se ni s izrekom da je „južni tužniji“. Za nju su „hrabre snage Juga“ dokaz da se i na jugu može raditi „zagrebački, svjetski, metropolitanski“. Ana zaključuje da tema i nije metropolitanska, nego svjetska. S tom se ocjenom gošća rado slaže.
sections.subtitle_en: From Dubrovnik to Mostar via Zagrebačka Ulica: A Conversation About Women's Health Begins with a Joke
sections.screenshot_description_en: Ana Pavlović in the studio asks Mirna Sentić through laughter why she planned to drive for six hours
sections.content_en:
The new episode of the podcast **„Rastući s djecom“** begins with a series of clips that immediately reveal the tone of the conversation. Mention is made of coffees that „boost“ cortisol, ovulation inhibited by stress, and the thought that parenthood does not begin with a plus on a test, but with the idea of two people becoming parents.

Host **Ana Pavlović** then announces that the episode is dedicated to women and women's health. She notes that this is also an opportunity for men who want to better understand how hormones affect women. She emphasizes that the central question is not only how hormones affect us, but also how we can affect them. That is precisely why the guest is not an endocrinologist, but nutritionist **Mirna Sentić**.

The conversation started only after technical difficulties and „numerous complications“ surrounding the arrangement itself. Ana does not miss the chance to joke at the guest's expense. Namely, Mirna had planned to travel as much as six hours from Dubrovnik to Mostar. The explanation is charming: the studio is located on **Zagrebačka ulica**, and the Dubrovnik–Zagreb route takes exactly six hours. „Those are my hormones,“ Mirna replies through laughter.

She adds that her logic was simple: when it comes to good guests, „everything happens in the Big City,“ so it must be Zagreb. Nor does she agree with the saying that „the south is sadder.“ For her, the „brave forces of the South“ are proof that even in the south one can work in a way that is „Zagreb-style, world-class, metropolitan.“ Ana concludes that the topic is not metropolitan, but global. The guest gladly agrees with that assessment.

sections.subtitle: Svako raspoloženje ima svoj hormon
sections.screenshot_description: Mirna Sentić objašnjava razliku između brzog i sporog djelovanja hormona i neurotransmitera
sections.content:
Prvo pitanje voditeljice provokativno je i izravno: jesmo li doista toliko pod utjecajem hormona ili se njima ponekad, onako, izvlačimo?

Mirna Sentić odgovara da je **svako raspoloženje uvjetovano nekim hormonom ili neurotransmiterom**. Priznaje da uvijek možemo pronaći „excuse“, odnosno opravdanje. No, ključ je u tome da razumijemo pravu svrhu svakog hormona. Kao primjere navodi:

- **inzulin**, hormon sitosti o kojem će se još govoriti,
- **serotonin**, „hormon sreće“, odnosno neurotransmiter,
- **dopamin**.

Sve su to, objašnjava gošća, podražaji iznutra koje mozak prima kao informaciju. Neki putuju trenutačno, a neki kronično, kroz vrijeme. Primjer sporijeg djelovanja je menstrualni ciklus. Estrogen polako raste do ovulacije, zatim pada, potom raste progesteron, pa i on pada. U toj fazi žene postaju nervozne. Takvim hormonima treba više vremena, a žene osjećaju i njihov rast i njihov pad.

S druge strane, dopaminske i adrenalinske reakcije su instantne. One donose ushićenje i jaku, trenutačnu reakciju.
sections.subtitle_en: Every Mood Has Its Hormone
sections.screenshot_description_en: Mirna Sentić explains the difference between the fast and slow action of hormones and neurotransmitters
sections.content_en:
The host's first question is provocative and direct: are we really under the influence of hormones that much, or do we sometimes sort of use them as an excuse?

Mirna Sentić responds that **every mood is conditioned by some hormone or neurotransmitter**. She admits that we can always find an „excuse,“ that is, a justification. But the key is for us to understand the true purpose of each hormone. As examples she cites:

- **insulin**, the satiety hormone that will be discussed further,
- **serotonin**, the „happiness hormone,“ that is, a neurotransmitter,
- **dopamine**.

All of these, the guest explains, are internal stimuli that the brain receives as information. Some travel instantaneously, and some chronically, over time. An example of slower action is the menstrual cycle. Estrogen slowly rises until ovulation, then drops, then progesterone rises, and it too drops. In that phase women become irritable. Such hormones take more time, and women feel both their rise and their fall.

On the other hand, dopamine and adrenaline reactions are instant. They bring exhilaration and a strong, immediate reaction.

sections.subtitle: „Pusti me, u PMS-u sam“: od izgovora do upravljanja hormonima
sections.screenshot_description: Mirna Sentić govori o cirkadijalnom ritmu i izmjeni melatonina i kortizola
sections.content:
Ana Pavlović iskreno priznaje da je i sama nekad bila tip osobe koja kaže: „Pusti me, sad sam u PMS-u.“ Ne poriče da hormonsko stanje mijenja doživljaj svijeta. Ipak, želi naglasiti ono što žene mogu učiniti kako bi one upravljale hormonima, a ne hormoni njima. Smatra da se hormoni mogu dovesti u balans. Tada smo „svoji“ i znamo što nam treba. Takvo stanje opisuje kao svojevrsni zen do kojeg treba doći.

Mirna Sentić polazi od temelja: **cirkadijalni ritam**, odnosno budnost i san, diktiraju hormoni. **Melatonin i kortizol** izmjenjuju se kao dan i noć. Kad poznajemo njihove zakonitosti, možemo predvidjeti i posljedice svojih odluka.

Ako si uskraćujemo san, logično je da ćemo biti umorni. Melatonin nije odradio svoj posao, nije nas odmorio, a jetra nije obavila detoksifikaciju. Sljedeći dan imamo manje energije jer smo se manje oporavili. Tada će, kaže gošća, **kortizol tražiti pomoć u inzulinu**. Čovjek je zato cijeli dan gladniji, jer mu se zapravo spava. Nema drugog načina da nadoknadi energiju nego da je pojede.

Podsjeća i da su kalorije zapravo energija. Poziva se na zakon prema kojem energija ne može nestati, nego samo mijenja oblik. Ako energiju nismo pojeli, ne možemo je dobiti „solarno“. Zato brojne prehrambene navike, zaključuje, izviru iz pitanja odlazimo li na vrijeme spavati i koliko se stresiramo.
sections.subtitle_en: „Leave Me Alone, I'm PMSing“: From Excuses to Managing Hormones
sections.screenshot_description_en: Mirna Sentić talks about the circadian rhythm and the alternation of melatonin and cortisol
sections.content_en:
Ana Pavlović frankly admits that she herself used to be the type of person who says: „Leave me alone, right now I'm PMSing.“ She does not deny that the hormonal state alters the experience of the world. Still, she wants to emphasize what women can do so that they manage hormones, rather than hormones managing them. She believes that hormones can be brought into balance. Then we are „ourselves“ and we know what we need. She describes such a state as a kind of zen that needs to be reached.

Mirna Sentić starts from the basics: **circadian rhythm**, that is, wakefulness and sleep, are dictated by hormones. **Melatonin and cortisol** alternate like day and night. When we know their regularities, we can also predict the consequences of our decisions.

If we deprive ourselves of sleep, it is logical that we will be tired. Melatonin has not done its job, it has not rested us, and the liver has not carried out detoxification. The next day we have less energy because we recovered less. Then, says the guest, **cortisol will look for help in insulin**. A person is therefore hungrier all day, because they are actually sleepy. There is no other way to replenish energy than to eat it.

She also reminds that calories are actually energy. She invokes the law according to which energy cannot disappear, but only changes form. If we haven't eaten the energy, we cannot get it „solarly.“ That is why numerous dietary habits, she concludes, stem from the question of whether we go to sleep on time and how much we stress ourselves out.

sections.subtitle: Tri kave do podne i kortizol na „boostu“
sections.screenshot_description: Mirna Sentić s osmijehom podiže šalicu kave dok objašnjava utjecaj kofeina na jutarnji kortizol
sections.content:
Jutarnji kortizol, objašnjava Mirna Sentić, trebao bi lijepo i postupno rasti otprilike od osam ili devet sati, sve do podneva. Tada doseže vrhunac, a s njim i najveću budnost. To je prirodan proces u kojem smo dobro stimulirani, kao što i treba biti.

Problem nastaje kad se umiješa kofein. „Bogu hvala, na Balkanu smo, pa jedna kava, druga kava, do podne mi smo s tri kave barem“, slikovito kaže gošća. Kortizol tada nema prirodan, polagan rast, nego ga „boostamo“. Poanta je, ističe, da prehrambenim i životnim navikama možemo poštovati ili narušavati te hormonske zakonitosti.

Pritom inzistira da ovo **nije blaćenje kofeina**. Nazdravlja kavom uz „U to ime, živjele!“ i dodaje da je kofein super stimulativna molekula. Svatko ga, međutim, drugačije metabolizira. Netko ima puno jaču reakciju, a netko slabiju, ovisno o enzimima u jetri i genetskoj predispoziciji.

Ipak, pravo stanje budnosti i umora, tvrdi, osjeća se tek kad se kofein makne iz igre i umor „dođe na naplatu“.
sections.subtitle_en: Three Coffees by Noon and Cortisol on a „Boost“
sections.screenshot_description_en: Mirna Sentić raises a coffee cup with a smile while explaining the effect of caffeine on morning cortisol
sections.content_en:
Morning cortisol, explains Mirna Sentić, should rise nicely and gradually from approximately eight or nine o'clock all the way until noon. Then it reaches its peak, and with it the greatest wakefulness. That is a natural process in which we are well stimulated, as it should be.

The problem arises when caffeine gets involved. „Thank God, we are in the Balkans, so one coffee, another coffee, by noon we're on at least three coffees,“ the guest vividly says. Cortisol then does not have a natural, slow rise; instead, we „boost“ it. The point is, she emphasizes, that through dietary and lifestyle habits we can respect or disrupt these hormonal regularities.

At the same time she insists that this **is not a smear on caffeine**. She toasts with coffee saying „To that, cheers!“ and adds that caffeine is a super-stimulating molecule. Everyone, however, metabolizes it differently. Someone has a much stronger reaction, and someone a weaker one, depending on liver enzymes and genetic predisposition.

Still, the true state of alertness and fatigue, she asserts, is felt only when caffeine is removed from the game and fatigue „comes due.“

sections.subtitle: Dvodnevni reset: ustajanje u pet, spavanje u deset, bez kofeina
sections.screenshot_description: Ana Pavlović u nevjerici ponavlja upute o ustajanju u 5 sati, a Mirna Sentić potvrđuje
sections.content:
Mirna Sentić iznosi recept za „resetiranje“ hormona koji i sama naziva pomalo ekstremnim. Prema njezinim riječima, isproban je „sto puta“. Sastoji se od tri koraka:

- **ustajanje u pet ujutro**, kako bi se stvorio prirodni umor,
- **odlazak na spavanje oko deset navečer**,
- **dva dana bez kofeina**.

Ta dva dana treba „stvarno preživjeti“, ali treći je dan, uvjerava gošća, čovjek resetiran. Ana Pavlović iskreno priznaje da to nikad nije probala. Gošća odgovara: „Teško je, teško je“, i dodaje da je metoda posebno korisna ženama koje žele resetirati hormone.

Zašto baš oko deset? Prirodni umor, objašnjava Mirna, javlja se kad počne padati mrak. Tada bi se melatonin trebao polako sintetizirati i početi nas odmarati. Umjesto toga, ljudi su i dalje izloženi **plavoj svjetlosti**, scrollaju i daju mozgu impulse da ostane budan. Njezin je savjet sve prigušiti i tijelu dopustiti reparaciju, kako bi se ponašalo prirodno, onako kako bi i trebalo.
sections.subtitle_en: Two-Day Reset: Getting Up at Five, Sleeping at Ten, No Caffeine
sections.screenshot_description_en: Ana Pavlović in disbelief repeats the instructions about getting up at 5 o'clock, and Mirna Sentić confirms
sections.content_en:
Mirna Sentić presents a recipe for „resetting“ hormones that she herself calls somewhat extreme. According to her words, it has been tested „a hundred times.“ It consists of three steps:

- **getting up at five in the morning**, in order to create natural fatigue,
- **going to sleep around ten in the evening**,
- **two days without caffeine**.

Those two days one must „truly survive,“ but on the third day, the guest assures, a person is reset. Ana Pavlović frankly admits that she has never tried it. The guest replies: „It's hard, it's hard,“ and adds that the method is especially useful for women who want to reset hormones.

Why around ten specifically? Natural fatigue, explains Mirna, appears when darkness begins to fall. Then melatonin should slowly be synthesized and begin resting us. Instead, people are still exposed to **blue light**, scrolling and giving the brain impulses to stay awake. Her advice is to dim everything and allow the body repair, so that it behaves naturally, the way it should.

sections.subtitle: Nježniji put: čaj umjesto kave i kava uz obrok
sections.screenshot_description: Mirna Sentić objašnjava zašto osobe s inzulinskom rezistencijom kavu trebaju „poljubiti“ uz obrok
sections.content:
Na Anino pitanje što je s glavoboljom koja prati odvikavanje od kave, Mirna Sentić odgovara da postoji i blaži, postupniji put. Riječ „odvikavanje“, moli kroz smijeh, treba staviti pod navodnike, da se kontekst ne bi krivo shvatio.

Alternativa su **crni i zeleni čajevi**. Biljka *Camellia sinensis* sadrži oblik kofeina koji se naziva **tein**. Djeluje jednako stimulativno, ali uz to donosi i obilje antioksidansa. Njegovo je djelovanje nježnije od kofeina iz kave, koji je puno koncentriraniji.

Ni sama gošća ne odriče se kave. Pije **jednu dnevno, i to uz obrok**. Objašnjava da kava s mlijekom tijelu daje impuls: inzulin reagira na mlijeko ili na šećer iz kave i stvara skok. Zato osobama s **inzulinskom rezistencijom** savjetuje da kavu „poljube“ uz obrok. Tako će im drugačije „pasti na tijelo“.

Ana dijeli vlastito iskustvo. Budući da kasno dolazi kući, kavu pije odmah nakon ručka, jer je u sedam ili osam navečer više ne želi piti. Primijetila je da joj takva kombinacija bolje odgovara. Nije, međutim, razmišljala da bi to moglo biti i bolje za organizam. Kroz smijeh zaključuje da je razgovor krenuo „udarno s kavom“. Imala je pripremljene papire s uvodom, a gošća ih je „odmah uvela u sve“.
sections.subtitle_en: A Gentler Path: Tea Instead of Coffee and Coffee with a Meal
sections.screenshot_description_en: Mirna Sentić explains why people with insulin resistance should „kiss“ coffee with a meal
sections.content_en:
To Ana's question about what to do with the headache that accompanies weaning off coffee, Mirna Sentić replies that there is also a milder, more gradual path. The word „weaning,“ she asks through laughter, should be put in quotation marks, lest the context be misunderstood.

The alternative is **black and green teas**. The plant *Camellia sinensis* contains a form of caffeine called **theine**. It has an equally stimulating effect, but in addition brings an abundance of antioxidants. Its action is gentler than the caffeine from coffee, which is much more concentrated.

The guest herself does not give up coffee either. She drinks **one a day, and with a meal**. She explains that coffee with milk gives the body an impulse: insulin reacts to the milk or to the sugar from the coffee and creates a spike. That is why she advises people with **insulin resistance** to „kiss“ coffee with a meal. That way it will „fall on the body“ differently.

Ana shares her own experience. Since she comes home late, she drinks coffee immediately after lunch, because at seven or eight in the evening she no longer wants to drink it. She noticed that this combination suits her better. She did not, however, think that it could also be better for the body. Through laughter she concludes that the conversation started „forcefully with coffee.“ She had prepared papers with an introduction, and the guest „immediately introduced them into everything.“

sections.subtitle: Nijedna namirnica nije zlo, ali hrana može biti okidač
sections.screenshot_description: Mirna Sentić nabraja metabolička stanja poput inzulinske rezistencije, PCOS-a i predijabetesa
sections.content:
Ana Pavlović otvara pitanje koje sve češće čuje. Zašto ljudima smeta mlijeko u kavi, zašto sve više njih pije crnu kavu i zašto je sve više intolerancija?

Mirna Sentić upozorava da je teško generalizirati. Kroz cijeli razgovor želi poručiti da hranu treba **naučiti poštovati**. „Ništa od namirnica nije zlo“, ističe. Postoje, međutim, metaboličke predispozicije i stanja koja su upisana u genetski kod:

- inzulinska rezistencija,
- PCOS,
- menopauza,
- predijabetes,
- hiperinzulinemija.

Prehranom i životnim stilom ta se stanja „trigeriraju“. Hrana, dakle, sama po sebi nije problem, nego okidač. Gošća navodi primjere. Osobi s iritabilnim kolonom mlijeko je okidač za odlazak na WC. Osoba s inzulinskom rezistencijom koja slatkiš pojede izolirano, izvan obroka, bit će gladna već za sat vremena, iako je unijela dovoljno energije. Razlog je to što joj je inzulin ostao visoko.

Isto vrijedi i za kavu s mlijekom i šećerom kao jedini „obrok“ za dobro jutro. To je jedini energent koji tijelo dobije, pa djeluje kao da je netko tijelo „udario bičem“. Njezin je savjet: **„Dajte mu hranu.“** Radije kruh i protein, kako bi energija dugo gorjela.

Redoslijed je jasan. Najprije treba pojesti ono što tijelu treba: ugljikohidrate kao energiju, proteine da ta energija dugo gori i masti zbog užitka u okusu. Tek onda dolazi „ćejf“ uz kavu. Kofein, naglašava, nije esencijalni nutrijent, nego dodatak za užitak. Uz pravi „matriks hrane“ ni mlijeko u kavi neće biti okidač. Tijelo nema problem s hranom, nego s tim što **nema obroka**.

Ana se pronalazi u tome. Svaki se dan pita zašto je popodne toliko umorna i „izbičevana“, a dan počinje upravo stimulacijom, „bičevanjem“ same sebe.
sections.subtitle_en: No Food Item Is Evil, but Food Can Be a Trigger
sections.screenshot_description_en: Mirna Sentić lists metabolic conditions such as insulin resistance, PCOS, and prediabetes
sections.content_en:
Ana Pavlović raises a question she hears more and more often. Why does milk in coffee bother people, why are more and more people drinking black coffee, and why are there more and more intolerances?

Mirna Sentić cautions that it is difficult to generalize. Throughout the entire conversation she wants to convey the message that one must **learn to respect** food. „None of the foodstuffs are evil,“ she emphasizes. There are, however, metabolic predispositions and conditions written into the genetic code:

- insulin resistance,
- PCOS,
- menopause,
- prediabetes,
- hyperinsulinemia.

Through diet and lifestyle, these conditions are „triggered.“ Food, therefore, is not a problem in itself, but a trigger. The guest cites examples. For a person with irritable bowel, milk is a trigger to go to the toilet. A person with insulin resistance who eats a sweet in isolation, outside of a meal, will be hungry already in an hour, even though they took in enough energy. The reason is that their insulin remained high.

The same applies to coffee with milk and sugar as the only „meal“ for good morning. That is the only energy source the body gets, so it acts as if someone „struck the body with a whip.“ Her advice is: **„Give it food.“** Rather bread and protein, so that the energy burns for a long time.

The order is clear. First, one should eat what the body needs: carbohydrates as energy, proteins so that this energy burns for a long time, and fats for the pleasure of taste. Only then comes the „ćejf“ with coffee. Caffeine, she emphasizes, is not an essential nutrient, but an additive for pleasure. With the right „food matrix,“ even milk in coffee will not be a trigger. The body does not have a problem with food, but with the fact that **there is no meal**.

Ana finds herself in this. Every day she asks herself why in the afternoon she is so tired and „whipped,“ yet starts the day precisely with stimulation, „whipping“ herself.

sections.subtitle: Ovulacija kao vrhunac nutritivnog statusa
sections.screenshot_description: Mirna Sentić objašnjava da su plodnost i ovulacija vrhunac ženskog zdravlja
sections.content:
Ana Pavlović primjećuje da se sredinom tridesetih godina počinju javljati brojne dijagnoze. Istodobno, to je razdoblje u kojem su žene i dalje plodne i možda pripremaju tijelo za prvu, drugu ili treću trudnoću. Ističe da je Mirna Sentić posebno posvećena temi kako prehranom i stilom života utjecati na ženske hormone, a posebno joj je u fokusu **PCOS**. Na pitanje je li to isto što i policistični jajnici, gošća kratko odgovara: „To je samo izgled.“ Najavljuje da je to tema za poseban dio razgovora.

Najprije želi dati širu sliku. Ideja njezina rada jest da **hrana bude u službi zdravlja i podrške plodnosti**. Ključna rečenica glasi: **plodnost i ovulacija vrhunac su našeg nutritivnog statusa**. Kad žena može dati kvalitetnu jajnu stanicu, oploditi se, iznijeti zdravu trudnoću i uspostaviti dojenje, tada je na vrhuncu zdravlja.

S menopauzom, kada estrogen „ode iz sustava kao da je magija“, počinje razgradnja. Tada, kaže gošća, **lifestyle dolazi na naplatu**. Pitanje je koliko se čuvamo da ta razgradnja ne krene prerano. Cilj je izgraditi koštano-mišićnu masu. Vršna koštana masa gradi se do tridesete godine, a reproduktivna faza traje od ranih dvadesetih do četrdesetih, pa i pedesetih, ovisno o tome kako se tko održava.

Životni stil, ističe, doslovno se vidi u **kvaliteti jajnih stanica i spermija**, odnosno u tome koliko smo nutrijenata uspjeli zadržati. Usporedbu pronalazi u prirodi. Biljka u sjemenci čuva klicu i novi život, a sjeme bačeno na plodno tlo dat će plod. Jajna stanica na isti se način čuva prehranom, snom i načinom života. Ana tome dodaje kretanje i stres, a Mirna oksidaciju.
sections.subtitle_en: Ovulation as the Peak of Nutritional Status
sections.screenshot_description_en: Mirna Sentić explains that fertility and ovulation are the peak of women's health
sections.content_en:
Ana Pavlović observes that in one's mid-thirties numerous diagnoses begin to appear. At the same time, this is a period in which women are still fertile and perhaps preparing the body for a first, second, or third pregnancy. She emphasizes that Mirna Sentić is particularly dedicated to the topic of how to influence female hormones through diet and lifestyle, and in her focus is especially **PCOS**. To the question of whether this is the same as polycystic ovaries, the guest replies briefly: „That is only appearance.“ She announces that this is a topic for a separate part of the conversation.

First, she wants to provide the broader picture. The idea of her work is for **food to be in service of health and support of fertility**. The key sentence is: **fertility and ovulation are the peak of our nutritional status**. When a woman can produce a quality egg cell, become fertilized, carry to term a healthy pregnancy, and establish breastfeeding, then she is at the peak of health.

With menopause, when estrogen „leaves the system as if it were magic,“ breakdown begins. Then, says the guest, **lifestyle comes due**. The question is how much we take care of ourselves so that this breakdown does not start too early. The goal is to build bone-muscle mass. Peak bone mass is built up to age thirty, and the reproductive phase lasts from the early twenties into the forties, and even fifties, depending on how each person maintains themselves.

Lifestyle, she emphasizes, is literally visible in the **quality of egg cells and sperm**, that is, in how many nutrients we have managed to retain. She finds a comparison in nature. A plant preserves the germ and new life in the seed, and seed cast on fertile ground will yield fruit. The egg cell is preserved in the same way through nutrition, sleep, and way of life. Ana adds movement and stress to this, and Mirna adds oxidation.

sections.subtitle: Inzulin, baterija našeg tijela
sections.screenshot_description: Mirna Sentić objašnjava što se događa kad je inzulin prestimuliran
sections.content:
Nakon šire slike, Mirna Sentić „zumira“ na jedan hormon. **Glavni hormon sitosti jest inzulin.** Uspoređuje ga s indikatorom baterije na mobitelu: on govori koliko energije imamo u sustavu.

Inzulinu cilj nije da stalno radi, nego da donese energiju i pospremi je u stanicu. Kad stalno grickamo, jedemo procesuiranu hranu, preskačemo obroke dva ili tri puta, a onda ga „zbubamo“ jednim velikim obrokom, inzulin izgubi ritam.

Ovulacija je, naglašava gošća, prirodni dar koji se sam događa. Zadatak je ukloniti „šumove“ koji su se nakupili u hormonima, a jedan od njih je **prestimulirani inzulin**. Gotovo sve hormonske disbalanse spomenute u razgovoru, poput **endometrioze, PCOS-a, menopauze i Hashimota**, prema njezinim riječima treba najprije nutritivno tretirati, i to balansiranjem inzulina kroz dan.

Prvi je korak dovoljno proteina ujutro. Inzulin će se lijepo lučiti kad obrok sadrži dovoljno proteina, uz ugljikohidrate te masti i vlakna koji sve to balansiraju.
sections.subtitle_en: Insulin, the Battery of Our Body
sections.screenshot_description_en: Mirna Sentić explains what happens when insulin is prestimulated
sections.content_en:
After the broader picture, Mirna Sentić „zooms in“ on one hormone. **The main satiety hormone is insulin.** She compares it to a battery indicator on a mobile phone: it tells how much energy we have in the system.

The goal of insulin is not to work constantly, but to deliver energy and store it in the cell. When we graze constantly, eat processed food, skip meals two or three times, and then „slam“ it with one large meal, insulin loses its rhythm.

Ovulation, the guest emphasizes, is a natural gift that happens on its own. The task is to eliminate the „noise“ that has accumulated in the hormones, and one of those is **prestimulated insulin**. Almost all hormonal imbalances mentioned in the conversation, such as **endometriosis, PCOS, menopause, and Hashimoto's**, according to her words should first be treated nutritionally, namely by balancing insulin throughout the day.

The first step is sufficient protein in the morning. Insulin will secrete nicely when a meal contains sufficient protein, along with carbohydrates and fats and fibers that balance it all.

sections.subtitle: Tanjur kao kamin: cjepanica, pruće i papir
sections.screenshot_description: Mirna Sentić rukama dočarava metaforu kamina i cjepanice dok objašnjava slaganje tanjura
sections.content:
Mirna Sentić zatim donosi metaforu koja, kaže, „uvijek upali“. Kad slažete tanjur, zamislite da je ispred vas **kamin**. Želite li se dobro ugrijati, treba vam:

- **Debela cjepanica, a to su proteini.** Gošća poziva da se zamisle jaja, riba, meso, mahunarke ili mliječni proizvodi. Bez cjepanice vatra ne može dugo gorjeti.
- **Pruće, a to su masti.** One pomažu da vatra dulje traje. Masni obrok ostaje u želucu dva do tri sata i dugo „tinja“.
- **Papir, a to su ugljikohidrati.** Oni služe za potpalu. Tanki papir gori brzo i odgovara jednostavnim ugljikohidratima. Debeli papir, primjerice karton, složeni su ugljikohidrati.

Na Anino pitanje znači li to da i po količini cjepanice treba biti najviše, gošća potvrđuje: „Tako je.“
sections.subtitle_en: The Plate as a Fireplace: Log, Kindling, and Paper
sections.screenshot_description_en: Mirna Sentić uses her hands to illustrate the metaphor of a fireplace and a log while explaining plate composition
sections.content_en:
Mirna Sentić then brings a metaphor that, she says, „always works.“ When assembling a plate, imagine that in front of you is a **fireplace**. If you want to warm up well, you need:

- **A thick log, and that is proteins.** The guest invites one to imagine eggs, fish, meat, legumes, or dairy products. Without a log, the fire cannot burn for long.
- **Kindling, and that is fats.** They help the fire last longer. A fatty meal stays in the stomach for two to three hours and „smolders“ for a long time.
- **Paper, and that is carbohydrates.** They serve for kindling. Thin paper burns quickly and corresponds to simple carbohydrates. Thick paper, for instance cardboard, is complex carbohydrates.

To Ana's question of whether this means that by quantity the log should also be the largest, the guest confirms: „That's right.“

sections.subtitle: „Jedi ko Mercedese“: tanjur u trećinama i manje ugljikohidrata navečer
sections.screenshot_description: Mirna Sentić rukom crta znak Mercedesa kako bi objasnila podjelu tanjura na trećine
sections.content:
Mirna Sentić podsjeća na službeno pravilo struke poznato kao **„my plate“**: pola tanjura vlakna, četvrtina proteini, četvrtina ugljikohidrati. To je, kaže, temelj balansirane prehrane.

Ljudima, međutim, voli predložiti i jednostavniju verziju, **trećine**. Tanjur se dijeli poput znaka mira ili znaka Mercedesa. Kroz šalu dodaje da će Mercedes morati staviti za sponzora emisije. Njezina poruka glasi: „Jedi ko Mercedese.“ Tako je, kaže, ljudima lakše zapamtiti.

Posebno je važan **smiraj dana**, osobito za osobe s problemom inzulina. Navečer se inzulin ne želi provocirati, jer tijelo tada treba odmarati, a ne probavljati. Zato savjetuje da se ugljikohidratni dio „ukrade“ s trećine na četvrtinu ili čak šestinu. Inzulin će tako odmoriti i vratiti se na bazalne vrijednosti.

Znak da je inzulin pod kontrolom jest **prirodna jutarnja glad** i izostanak one „lude gladi“ navečer, kada se nešto želi grickati. Ana to naziva žudnjama. Gošća objašnjava da su one poruka inzulina: „Nisi me nahranio ujutro jer si preskočio, nije bilo dovoljno energije, a ja te sad tražim.“
sections.subtitle_en: „Eat Like Mercedes“: The Plate in Thirds and Fewer Carbohydrates in the Evening
sections.screenshot_description_en: Mirna Sentić draws a Mercedes sign with her hand to explain dividing the plate into thirds
sections.content_en:
Mirna Sentić recalls the official professional rule known as **„my plate“**: half the plate fiber, a quarter protein, a quarter carbohydrates. That, she says, is the foundation of a balanced diet.

To people, however, she likes to propose an even simpler version, **thirds**. The plate is divided like a peace sign or the Mercedes emblem. Through a joke she adds that they will have to make Mercedes a sponsor of the show. Her message is: „Eat like Mercedes.“ That way, she says, it is easier for people to remember.

Especially important is the **calm of the day**, particularly for people with an insulin problem. In the evening one does not want to provoke insulin, because the body then needs to rest, not digest. Therefore she advises that the carbohydrate portion be „stolen“ from a third to a fourth or even a sixth. Insulin will thus rest and return to basal values.

A sign that insulin is under control is **natural morning hunger** and the absence of that „crazy hunger“ in the evening, when one wants to snack on something. Ana calls these cravings. The guest explains that they are insulin's message: „You didn't feed me in the morning because you skipped, there wasn't enough energy, and now I'm asking you for it.“

sections.subtitle: Borba hormona i karaktera: večernje žudnje i prerađena hrana
sections.screenshot_description: Mirna Sentić govori o povratku kuhanju kod kuće i tvorničkim postavkama
sections.content:
Ana Pavlović večernje žudnje opisuje kao **„borbu između hormona i karaktera“**. Ako hormonima tijekom dana nismo dali ono što im treba, navečer je samo pitanje hoće li pobijediti žudnja.

Mirna Sentić to pojednostavljuje na energiju. Tijelo dobiva kalorije iz masti, proteina i ugljikohidrata. To je, kaže, „fenomenalno priroda smislila“, jer su ljudi nekad jeli ono što su našli i skupili, a ne balansirano. Ana dodaje da tada nije bilo prerađene hrane, pa je prehrana možda ipak bila uravnoteženija. Gošća se slaže: danas su „provokacije drugačije“, a **aditivi u hrani** dodatno provociraju inzulin.

Zato ljude vraća na „tvorničke postavke“, odnosno na **vještine kuhanja** i pripremu hrane kod kuće. Na taj način jača svijest o tome gdje je problem. Raznolikost je, smatra, najmanji problem u ovom „svijetu obilja“, jer ljudi doista raznoliko jedu. Problem su **količine i omjeri na tanjuru**.

Drugi problem je to što su dnevne obveze postale prioritetnije od tjelesnih potreba. Glad bi trebalo shvaćati kao nuždu, jednako važnu kao mokrenje. Umjesto toga, ljudi posegnu za kavom ili slatkišem i potrebu odgađaju po principu „delay, ask me later“. Taj „later“, upozorava gošća, stigne s 35, 36 ili 37 godina, kad jetra više ne može sve tako brzo odrađivati.
sections.subtitle_en: The Battle of Hormones and Character: Evening Cravings and Processed Food
sections.screenshot_description_en: Mirna Sentić talks about returning to cooking at home and factory settings
sections.content_en:
Ana Pavlović describes evening cravings as a **„battle between hormones and character“**. If we did not give hormones what they need during the day, in the evening it is only a question of whether the craving will win.

Mirna Sentić simplifies this to energy. The body gets calories from fats, proteins, and carbohydrates. That is, she says, „a phenomenal invention of nature,“ because people once ate what they found and gathered, not in a balanced way. Ana adds that back then there was no processed food, so the diet was perhaps more balanced after all. The guest agrees: today „provocations are different,“ and **food additives** additionally provoke insulin.

That is why she returns people to „factory settings,“ that is, to **cooking skills** and preparing food at home. In this way, awareness of where the problem lies is strengthened. Variety is, she believes, the least problem in this „world of abundance,“ because people truly eat a variety. The problem is **quantities and proportions on the plate**.

Another problem is that daily obligations have become more of a priority than physical needs. Hunger should be understood as a physiological need, just as important as urination. Instead, people reach for coffee or a sweet and postpone the need according to the principle of „delay, ask me later.“ That „later,“ warns the guest, arrives at age 35, 36, or 37, when the liver can no longer process everything so quickly.

sections.subtitle: Svako peto dijete pretilo, a kronične bolesti dolaze u tridesetima
sections.screenshot_description: Mirna Sentić prepričava riječi profesorice o generaciji koja možda neće živjeti dulje od roditelja
sections.content:
Ana Pavlović otkriva da je podcast pokrenula s fokusom na djecu. S vremenom se taj fokus sve više pomicao prema roditeljima, jer ako su roditelji dobro, s djecom će biti lako. Djeca od njih preuzimaju i prehrambene navike i odnos prema sebi i drugima.

Spominje zabrinjavajuće brojke o pretilosti djece. U njezinoj županiji, koliko se sjeća, pretilo je **svako peto dijete**. Pita se zašto, ali i zašto se sve češće čuju dijagnoze poput Hashimota „kod svake druge žene“. Kod muškaraca se, dodaje, srčani problemi i visok tlak javljaju već u tridesetima. To su nekad bile bolesti ljudi starijih od šezdeset. Njezina generacija, ističe, već je odrastala na drukčijoj prehrani od svojih roditelja: salamama, prerađevinama i brzoj hrani nakon izlazaka. Sve to sada „dolazi na naplatu“.

Mirna Sentić ne voli to gledati kao kaznu, nego kao račun: kako ga platiti, što promijeniti, gdje „dodatno zaraditi“. Djeca su, kaže, naš odraz, naše blago i naše sutra. Prisjeća se riječi profesorice s pete godine studija: **„Mi smo već generacija koja ne zna hoće li dulje živjeti od svojih roditelja.“** Kronične nezarazne bolesti javljaju se ranije zbog stresa, obveza i goleme količine informacija koje tijelo ne zna filtrirati.

Zato posao nutricionista, ističe, nije samo sastavljati jelovnike, jer to danas radi umjetna inteligencija. Posao je pomoći ljudima da razviju **kritički stav** i filtriraju informacije važne upravo za njih. Ana dodaje da je ključan individualni pristup.

Gošća naglašava da u svemu tome ne treba biti grižnje savjesti. Svi se hranimo, kao što svi odgajamo djecu, i svatko ima svoje metode. Prisjeća se vlastitog djetinjstva. Odrasla je u obitelji sa **šestero djece**, a roditelji su ih hranili Čokolinom i paštetama. To joj je potpuno razumljivo: „Mi smo bili sretna djeca. Nama ništa nije falilo.“ Ana dodaje da je ona dijete sa sela, gdje je kupovina salame bila doživljaj, a pršut je uvijek bio tu.

Mirna to povezuje s **nedostatkom stresa** u ono vrijeme. Kad je tijelo u stanju „fight or flight“, spušta se iz reproduktivnog moda u mod preživljavanja. Tada crpi resurse odakle može: iz jetre, iz jajnih stanica. Kad se tome pridruže pušenje, alkohol i nespavanje, tijelo „mora negdje uzeti danak“. Stres pritom ne dopušta stanici da se odmori, pa prirodni mehanizam popravka ne može djelovati.
sections.subtitle_en: Every Fifth Child Obese, and Chronic Diseases Arrive in the Thirties
sections.screenshot_description_en: Mirna Sentić retells the words of a professor about a generation that might not live longer than their parents
sections.content_en:
Ana Pavlović reveals that she launched the podcast with a focus on children. Over time, that focus shifted more and more toward parents, because if parents are well, it will be easy with the children. Children take from them both dietary habits and attitudes toward themselves and others.

She mentions worrying figures about childhood obesity. In her county, as far as she recalls, **every fifth child** is obese. She wonders why, but also why diagnoses like Hashimoto's are increasingly heard „in every second woman.“ In men, she adds, heart problems and high blood pressure appear already in their thirties. Those were once diseases of people older than sixty. Her generation, she emphasizes, already grew up on a different diet from their parents: salamis, processed meats, and fast food after going out. All of that is now „coming due.“

Mirna Sentić does not like to look at this as a punishment, but as a bill: how to pay it, what to change, where to „earn extra.“ Children are, she says, our reflection, our treasure, and our tomorrow. She recalls the words of a professor from her fifth year of studies: **„We are already a generation that does not know whether it will live longer than its parents.“** Chronic non-communicable diseases appear earlier due to stress, obligations, and a huge amount of information that the body does not know how to filter.

That is why a nutritionist's job, she emphasizes, is not just to compose menus, because artificial intelligence does that today. The job is to help people develop a **critical attitude** and filter information important precisely for them. Ana adds that an individual approach is crucial.

The guest emphasizes that in all of this there should be no guilt. We all nourish ourselves, just as we all raise children, and everyone has their own methods. She recalls her own childhood. She grew up in a family with **six children**, and her parents fed them Čokolino and pâtés. That is completely understandable to her: „We were happy children. We lacked nothing.“ Ana adds that she is a child from the village, where buying salami was an event, while prosciutto was always there.

Mirna connects this with the **lack of stress** at that time. When the body is in a state of „fight or flight,“ it drops from reproductive mode into survival mode. Then it draws resources from wherever it can: from the liver, from egg cells. When smoking, alcohol, and lack of sleep join that, the body „must take its toll somewhere.“ Stress in the process does not allow the cell to rest, so the natural repair mechanism cannot function.

sections.subtitle: Krivulje zdravlja i bogatstva: metafora o starenju
sections.screenshot_description: Mirna Sentić rukama crta krivulje zdravlja i imovine koje se sijeku
sections.content:
Kako bi slikovito opisala starenje, Mirna Sentić prepričava metaforu koju joj je dao **Mark Thomas iz Dubrovnika**. Opisuje ga kao Londonca koji je doselio u Dubrovnik i ondje se zaljubio, novinara po struci, planinara, čija je supruga vegetarijanka. Ističe da je čovjek s velikom razinom svijesti o životu. Metaforu joj je ponudio dok ju je pripremao za jedno izlaganje na engleskom jeziku.

Zamislite dva grafa, **health i wealth**, odnosno zdravlje i imovinsko stanje, a na osi X životni vijek:

- **Krivulja zdravlja** počinje na vrhuncu, jer se rađamo zdravi, i s vremenom ide prema dolje.
- **Krivulja bogatstva** počinje na dnu, jer se rađamo siromašni, pa polako stječemo sposobnost zarade i ona raste.

U nekom se trenutku te krivulje dodirnu. Na nama je da tada krivulju zdravlja ne pustimo da pada, nego da je „potegnemo“ udesno, u ravnu liniju. „E, to ti je starenje“, rekao joj je. Gošća priznaje da je pomislila: „Wow, ja ovo moram pričati ljudima.“

U mladosti tijelo je u izgradnji i puno nutrijenata, a jetra ima veći kapacitet. Zato je oporavak bio brz, a mamurluk kraći. Ana to potvrđuje primjerom: dovoljno je jedno vjenčanje nakon kojeg se tri dana ne možeš oporaviti i zapitaš se: „Kad se ovo dogodilo?“
sections.subtitle_en: Curves of Health and Wealth: A Metaphor for Aging
sections.screenshot_description_en: Mirna Sentić draws health and wealth curves with her hands that intersect
sections.content_en:
To vividly describe aging, Mirna Sentić retells a metaphor given to her by **Mark Thomas from Dubrovnik**. She describes him as a Londoner who moved to Dubrovnik and fell in love there, a journalist by profession, a hiker, whose wife is a vegetarian. She emphasizes that he is a man with a high level of awareness about life. He offered her the metaphor while preparing her for a presentation in English.

Imagine two graphs, **health and wealth**, that is, health and financial status, and on the X axis lifespan:

- **The health curve** starts at its peak, because we are born healthy, and over time goes downwards.
- **The wealth curve** starts at the bottom, because we are born poor, and we slowly acquire earning capacity and it grows.

At some point those curves touch. It is up to us then not to let the health curve fall, but to „pull“ it to the right, into a flat line. „Well, that's aging for you,“ he told her. The guest admits that she thought: „Wow, I have to talk to people about this.“

In youth the body is under construction and full of nutrients, and the liver has a greater capacity. That is why recovery was fast, and hangovers shorter. Ana confirms this with an example: one wedding is enough after which you cannot recover for three days and you ask yourself: „When did this happen?“

sections.subtitle: Mediteranski način života: kava u miru i zajednički obroci
sections.screenshot_description: Mirna Sentić govori o bazi mediteranske piramide: druženju, zajedničkim obrocima i pokretu
sections.content:
Mehanizmi održavanja i čuvanja resursa, prema Mirni Sentić, jednostavni su: **kava u miru, razgovori sa smislom i mediteranski način života**. U bazi mediteranske piramide nisu namirnice, nego:

- socijalizacija, druženje i dijeljenje iskustva,
- **zajednički obroci**, što s Anom zajednički naglašavaju,
- hidratacija,
- pokret.

Svjesna je da su danas svi za računalima i da ljudi nemaju potrebu kretati se. Dovoljno je, međutim, otići u šumu da se dobije osjećaj: „Ajme, napunio sam se.“

Njezin je pristup jačanje svijesti. Nekoga mijenjati, kaže, „suluda je izjava“, ali motivirati ga na promjenu navika i pokazati mu kako, to je moguće. Važno je definirati **nutritivne deficite** koje je osoba razvila. Neki su vidljivi u nalazima, a neki u simptomima poput kroničnog umora, teškog buđenja ili nesanice. Takvi se deficiti mogu „ušminkati“, ali treba vremena da osoba sama sebi prizna: „Bolje sam.“ Pritom je važno da nije u toksičnim odnosima, jer se može savršeno hraniti, ali ako je u toksičnoj okolini, to nije dovoljno.
sections.subtitle_en: The Mediterranean Lifestyle: Coffee in Peace and Shared Meals
sections.screenshot_description_en: Mirna Sentić speaks about the base of the Mediterranean pyramid: socializing, shared meals, and movement
sections.content_en:
Mechanisms of maintaining and preserving resources, according to Mirna Sentić, are simple: **coffee in peace, conversations with meaning, and the Mediterranean lifestyle**. At the base of the Mediterranean pyramid are not food items, but:

- socialization, hanging out, and sharing experiences,
- **shared meals**, which she and Ana jointly emphasize,
- hydration,
- movement.

She is aware that today everyone is at computers and that people have no need to move. It is enough, however, to go into the forest to get the feeling: „Oh, I've recharged.“

Her approach is raising awareness. Changing someone, she says, is „an insane statement,“ but motivating someone to change habits and showing them how, that is possible. It is important to define **nutritional deficits** that a person has developed. Some are visible in lab results, and some in symptoms such as chronic fatigue, difficulty waking up, or insomnia. Such deficits can be „dressed up,“ but it takes time for a person to admit to themselves: „I am better.“ At the same time it is important not to be in toxic relationships, because one can eat perfectly, but if one is in a toxic environment, that is not enough.

sections.subtitle: Kad stres utiša ovulaciju: prolaktin i kortizol
sections.screenshot_description: Mirna Sentić objašnjava kako povišeni prolaktin i kortizol suprimiraju ovulaciju
sections.content:
Na Anino pitanje vidi li se utjecaj toksične okoline i na hormonima, Mirna Sentić odgovara: „Kako ne, kako ne.“

Prvi primjer je **prolaktin**. Svi ostali hormoni mogu biti uredni, ali prolaktin, koji je u središtu i koordinira cijelu hormonsku hijerarhiju, bude „ogroman“. Tada suprimira ovulaciju i sve ostalo. Razlog može biti trauma, jak stres ili nešto drugo, primjerice **prolaktinom**.

Ponekad, priznaje gošća, učini se sve u životnom stilu i suplementaciji, a rezultata nema. Tada kaže: „Tu sad moj posao staje.“ Vrijeme je da se uključi **dobar endokrinolog** koji zna što je dotad napravljeno. Slijede farmakoterapija ili, ako je potrebno, kirurgija.

Drugi primjer je **kortizol**. Kad je on poremećen, poremećeni su i spolni hormoni, ali ne zato što s njima nešto nije u redu, nego zato što je žena pod jakim stresom. Kortizol ženi ne raste samo u akutnom stresu, nego i kad samo razmišlja kako će. Primjeri su egzistencijalna pitanja, poput gubitka posla u trenutku kad žele ostati trudne. Dovoljno je i da začeće ne uspije pet mjeseci pa se pojavi pitanje „što ako ne mogu?“. To je, kaže, **„dovoljno jako pitanje da kortizol radi svoj posao: suprimira ovulaciju“**.

Mnogi koji joj dolaze upravo su u toj fazi: izgubili su se i već su sami sebi definirali da „to neće moći prirodno“. **Strah i neizvjesnost**, naglašava, nisu emocije u kojima je žena reproduktivno sposobna. Prvi je korak promijeniti način razmišljanja u: „Kako ja mogu sudjelovati?“ Ana to sažima rečenicom: „Što mogu napraviti?“
sections.subtitle_en: When Stress Silences Ovulation: Prolactin and Cortisol
sections.screenshot_description_en: Mirna Sentić explains how elevated prolactin and cortisol suppress ovulation
sections.content_en:
To Ana's question of whether the influence of a toxic environment is also seen on hormones, Mirna Sentić replies: „Of course, of course.“

The first example is **prolactin**. All other hormones can be orderly, but prolactin, which is at the center and coordinates the entire hormonal hierarchy, is „huge.“ Then it suppresses ovulation and everything else. The reason can be trauma, severe stress, or something else, for example a **prolactinoma**.

Sometimes, the guest admits, everything is done in lifestyle and supplementation, yet there are no results. Then she says: „Here my job stops now.“ It is time to involve a **good endocrinologist** who knows what has been done up to that point. Pharmacotherapy follows or, if necessary, surgery.

The second example is **cortisol**. When it is disrupted, sex hormones are also disrupted, but not because something is wrong with them, but because the woman is under severe stress. Cortisol does not only rise in a woman in acute stress, but also when she is merely thinking about how she will manage. Examples are existential questions, such as job loss at the moment when they want to become pregnant. It is also enough for conception not to succeed for five months and the question „what if I can't?“ appears. That is, she says, **„a strong enough question for cortisol to do its job: suppress ovulation“**.

Many who come to her are precisely in that phase: they have lost themselves and have already defined for themselves that „they won't be able to do this naturally.“ **Fear and uncertainty**, she emphasizes, are not emotions in which a woman is reproductively capable. The first step is to change the mindset to: „How can I participate?“ Ana summarizes this with the sentence: „What can I do?“

sections.subtitle: Tražite liječnika koji vas čuje
sections.screenshot_description: Mirna Sentić poručuje ženama da ne odustaju dok ne pronađu liječnika koji ih čuje
sections.content:
Kad se krene u akciju, rad se najčešće usmjeri na prehranu, suplementaciju i stil života. Mirna Sentić poručuje: **„Svaki dan nešto možeš napraviti.“** Usporedno s tim, savjetuje, treba graditi povjerenje s endokrinologom i ginekologom koji te čuje.

Otvoreno govori o problemu u zdravstvu. Zbog golemog broja pacijenata liječnici ne mogu ostvariti dublji odnos s pacijentom. Netko tko dnevno primi sto ljudi ne može dati savjet na razini ljudskosti i dubine koja je potrebna. Zato mnogi kažu: „Nije me ni pogledao, nije me ni vidio.“ Gošća naglašava da to nije samo do liječnika, nego do **sustava koji liječniku ne dopušta da čuje pacijenta**.

Njezina je poruka svima koji se pitaju „kako ću, mogu li“, ili im je netko zalijepio etiketu „ti nećeš moći“: **ako niste zadovoljni liječnikom, ne stajte. Idite dalje dok ne pronađete osobu koja vas čuje.**
sections.subtitle_en: Look for a Doctor Who Hears You
sections.screenshot_description_en: Mirna Sentić tells women not to give up until they find a doctor who hears them
sections.content_en:
When taking action, work is most often focused on nutrition, supplementation, and lifestyle. Mirna Sentić says: **„Every day you can do something.“** In parallel with that, she advises, one should build trust with an endocrinologist and gynecologist who hears you.

She speaks openly about the problem in healthcare. Due to the huge number of patients, doctors cannot establish a deeper relationship with the patient. Someone who receives a hundred people a day cannot give advice at the level of humanity and depth that is needed. That is why many say: „He didn't even look at me, he didn't even see me.“ The guest emphasizes that this is not only up to the doctor, but down to **a system that does not allow the doctor to hear the patient**.

Her message to everyone who is asking themselves „how will I, can I,“ or has had someone slap the label on them „you won't be able to“: **if you are not satisfied with your doctor, do not stop. Keep going until you find a person who hears you.**

sections.subtitle: Sekundarna neplodnost: kad prva trudnoća uspije, a druga ne dolazi
sections.screenshot_description: Mirna Sentić objašnjava pojam sekundarne neplodnosti i važnost nutritivnog oporavka između trudnoća
sections.content:
Ana Pavlović otvara temu koju primjećuje u svom okruženju. Žene koje su već uspješno prošle jednu trudnoću ne uspijevaju zatrudnjeti drugi ili treći put. Znaju da mogu, vjeruju da će uspjeti, ali stres se ipak pojavi kad pokušavaju dulje vrijeme. Uvjerena je da je upravo hormon stresa tu ključan.

„U tom grmu leži zec“, potvrđuje Mirna Sentić. U dvadesetima smo bili „lakoumniji“, sve je bilo lakše, a priroda je osmislila da smo tada reproduktivno najjači. Prisjeća se riječi profesorice biologije: **„Bakteriji treba 20 minuta da se podijeli, a nama 20 godina.“** Dvadesete su najplodnije godine. Ipak, uvjeti života, prije svega egzistencijalna pitanja, otežavaju da se djeca imaju baš tada.

Ne želi ulaziti u to što je ispravno. Smatra da je djecu važno imati **kad je čovjek spreman i kad tijelo kaže „da“, koji god to broj bio**. Tijelu je s dvadeset godina lakše, jer ima drugačije mehanizme i nutritivne zalihe. U tridesetima, međutim, treba uzeti u obzir mnogo više čimbenika od same prehrane i suplementacije, koje se „daju namjestiti“. Važni su odnosi i vrijeme za sebe, kako bi se ušlo u **„reproduktivni mindset“**. Zato liječnici koji se bave reproduktivnim zdravljem često savjetuju: „Idite na odmor.“ Cilj je izaći iz svakodnevice i ne slušati pitanja tipa „kad će, što ne ide“. Ta pitanja, ponavlja gošća, ne služe ničemu. Nitko pritom nije kriv. Bolja je rečenica: „Kako ti mogu pomoći? Čula sam za nekoga tko ti može pomoći.“ To je, kažu obje, ono što žele: **žena ženi**.

Gošća posebno ističe Aninu rečenicu da je prvi put uspjelo. To je dokaz da je tijelo plodno. Takvo se stanje naziva **sekundarna neplodnost**. Najčešće nastaje jer nešto „šumi“ u hormonskom panelu. Šumilo je i prije, ali tijelo je to tada, mlađe, uspjelo nadići. Svaka nova trudnoća, što smo stariji, nutritivno je zahtjevnija i za postići i za održati.

Posebno upozorava na **postpartum**. Prisjeća se izreke kakvu bi rekla neka baka: „Izgubila sam zube s četvrtim djetetom.“ Negdje je, objašnjava, taj nutrijent morala dobiti. Što je kraći razmak između poroda i nove trudnoće, to je potrebno više za nutritivni oporavak. Ana to sažima u dvije riječi: **„Nema zaliha.“**
sections.subtitle_en: Secondary Infertility: When the First Pregnancy Succeeds, but the Second Does Not Come
sections.screenshot_description_en: Mirna Sentić explains the concept of secondary infertility and the importance of nutritional recovery between pregnancies
sections.content_en:
Ana Pavlović opens a topic she notices in her surroundings. Women who have already successfully gone through one pregnancy do not succeed in getting pregnant a second or third time. They know they can, they believe they will succeed, but stress nonetheless appears when they have been trying for a longer time. She is convinced that it is precisely the stress hormone that is key here.

„That's the rub,“ confirms Mirna Sentić. In our twenties we were „more carefree,“ everything was easier, and nature designed it so that we are reproductively strongest then. She recalls the words of a biology professor: **„It takes a bacterium 20 minutes to divide, and it takes us 20 years.“** The twenties are the most fertile years. Still, living conditions, primarily existential issues, make it harder to have children precisely then.

She does not want to go into what is right. She believes that it is important to have children **when a person is ready and when the body says „yes“, whatever that number may be**. For the body it is easier at twenty, because it has different mechanisms and nutritional stores. In the thirties, however, one must take into account many more factors than just diet and supplementation, which „can be adjusted.“ Relationships and time for oneself are important, in order to enter a **„reproductive mindset“**. That is why doctors who deal with reproductive health often advise: „Go on vacation.“ The goal is to get out of everyday routine and not listen to questions like „when is it going to happen, why isn't it working.“ Those questions, the guest repeats, serve no purpose. No one is to blame in this. A better sentence is: „How can I help you? I heard of someone who can help you.“ That is, both say, what they want: **woman to woman**.

The guest particularly highlights Ana's sentence that it worked the first time. That is proof that the body is fertile. Such a condition is called **secondary infertility**. Most often it occurs because something is „creating static“ in the hormonal panel. It was creating static before too, but the body then, younger, managed to overcome it. Each new pregnancy, as we get older, is nutritionally more demanding both to achieve and to maintain.

She specifically warns about the **postpartum** period. She recalls a saying that some grandmother would say: „I lost my teeth with the fourth child.“ Somewhere, she explains, she had to get that nutrient. The shorter the interval between delivery and a new pregnancy, the more is needed for nutritional recovery. Ana summarizes this in two words: **„No reserves.“**
