sections.subtitle: Od PCOS-a do PMOS-a: sindrom koji počinje daleko od jajnika
sections.screenshot_description: Mirna Sentić objašnjava novu terminologiju PMOS i zašto su jajnici tek treći u nazivu sindroma
sections.content:
Voditeljica **Ana Pavlović** otvara novo poglavlje razgovora pitanjem koje muči mnoge mlade žene. Dijagnoza policističnih jajnika ili sindroma, ponekad postavljena i prije dvadesete godine, odmah pokreće brige. Ana ipak naglašava da ta dijagnoza nije pravilo i da nije jedini problem koji kasnije može otežati začeće. Zato pita na koje simptome treba paziti od najranijih godina. Posebno misli na mladu djevojku koja ne planira trudnoću idući mjesec, ali je možda planira za pet godina. Zanima je kako se pripremiti i što tijelo u tom trenutku poručuje. Nutricionistica **Mirna Sentić** odgovara da to pitanje u sebi nose sve žene.

Gošća najprije pojašnjava nazive. Policistični ovarijski sindrom (PCOS) prema njezinim je riječima službena terminologija bio do 2026. godine, a sada se koristi naziv **PMOS**, odnosno *poliendokrinološki metabolički ovarijski sindrom*. Mirna ističe da je jajnik u tom nazivu tek na trećem mjestu. Riječ je o stanju u kojem više žlijezda metabolički narušava zdravlje, a posljedice se tek potom vide na jajniku i plodnosti.

Prema njezinu mišljenju upravo zato ginekolozi sindrom često ne prepoznaju na vrijeme. Promatraju ga samo kroz lupu jajnika i maternice, a potrebno je vrijeme da se na jajnicima pojave nezreli folikuli. Mirna objašnjava da osobe s pretilošću i inzulinskom rezistencijom imaju veći rizik za razvoj policističnog izgleda jajnika. Što je inzulin viši i manje reguliran, to više „guši“ jajnu stanicu u razvoju. Rezultat je mnoštvo jajnih stanica koje su trebale ovulirati, ali nisu, pa su ciklusi zbog izostanka ovulacije dugi.
sections.subtitle_en: From PCOS to PMOS: A Syndrome That Begins Far from the Ovaries
sections.screenshot_description_en: Mirna Sentić explains the new PMOS terminology and why the ovaries are only third in the name of the syndrome
sections.content_en:
Host **Ana Pavlović** opens a new chapter of the conversation with a question that troubles many young women. A diagnosis of polycystic ovaries or syndrome, sometimes made even before age twenty, immediately triggers worries. Ana nevertheless emphasizes that this diagnosis is not the rule and that it is not the only problem that can later make conception difficult. Therefore, she asks which symptoms one should watch out for from the earliest years. She specifically has in mind a young girl who is not planning a pregnancy next month, but might be planning one in five years. She wants to know how to prepare and what the body is communicating at that moment. Nutritionist **Mirna Sentić** answers that all women carry this question inside them.

The guest first clarifies the terms. Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), according to her words, was official terminology until 2026, and now the name **PMOS** is used, that is, *polyendocrinological metabolic ovarian syndrome*. Mirna emphasizes that the ovary is only in third place in that name. It is a condition in which multiple glands metabolically disrupt health, and the consequences are only then seen on the ovary and fertility.

In her view, that is precisely why gynecologists often do not recognize the syndrome in time. They observe it only through the lens of the ovary and uterus, and it takes time for immature follicles to appear on the ovaries. Mirna explains that individuals with obesity and insulin resistance have a higher risk of developing a polycystic appearance of the ovaries. The higher and less regulated the insulin is, the more it „suffocates“ the developing egg cell. The result is a multitude of egg cells that should have ovulated, but did not, so cycles are long due to the absence of ovulation.

sections.subtitle: Petnaest godina sa sindromom: osobni put do remisije
sections.screenshot_description: Mirna Sentić govori o vlastitom iskustvu s PCOS-om i sedam godina rada na remisiji
sections.content:
Razgovor tada postaje osoban. Mirna Sentić otkriva da i sama ima PCOS i da s njim živi već **15 godina**. Sedam od tih godina, kako kaže, „dovodila“ ga je u red, proučavala ga i upoznavala vlastitu cikličnost. Htjela je otkriti koliko prehranom, načinom života i suplementima koji joj čuvaju inzulin može taj hormon staviti pod kontrolu, kako bi njezini jajnici mogli nesmetano ovulirati.

Iz tog iskustva proizlazi rečenica koju često ponavlja klijenticama: **„Vama hormoni šume vašoj ovulaciji.“** Gošća je uvjerena da najčešći problem nije ginekološki. Kada se uspostavi ravnoteža, ovulacija se dogodi, menstruacija dođe, a ciklusi se skrate. To je, kaže, dokaz da je žena na dobrom putu prema remisiji. Sindrom pritom ne nestaje jer je zapisan u genetskom kodu, a geni prema njezinim riječima čine oko 40 do 50 posto onoga što jesmo.

Ana Pavlović zatim pita može li se taj genetski kod „upaliti“ u nekom trenutku ako ga prije nije bilo. Mirna potvrđuje da može. Okidači su prehrana i način života, odnosno područje **epigenetike**: način na koji živimo potiče određene gene da se drugačije izraze. Ana priznaje da se, s dvije trudnoće iza sebe, pita je li se nešto moglo razviti u međuvremenu, jer tijekom pripreme za trudnoću nije provjeravala stanje inzulina.
sections.subtitle_en: Fifteen Years with the Syndrome: A Personal Path to Remission
sections.screenshot_description_en: Mirna Sentić speaks about her own experience with PCOS and seven years of work toward remission
sections.content_en:
The conversation then becomes personal. Mirna Sentić reveals that she herself has PCOS and has been living with it for **15 years**. For seven of those years, as she says, she was „getting it in order,“ studying it, and getting to know her own cyclicity. She wanted to discover how much she could bring that hormone under control through diet, lifestyle, and supplements that preserve her insulin, so that her ovaries could ovulate unhindered.

From that experience comes a sentence she often repeats to female clients: **„Your hormones are creating static for your ovulation.“** The guest is convinced that the most common problem is not gynecological. When balance is established, ovulation occurs, menstruation arrives, and cycles shorten. That, she says, is proof that a woman is on the right path toward remission. The syndrome does not disappear in the process because it is written in the genetic code, and genes, according to her words, make up about 40 to 50 percent of what we are.

Ana Pavlović then asks whether that genetic code can be „switched on“ at some point if it was not present before. Mirna confirms that it can. The triggers are diet and lifestyle, that is, the field of **epigenetics**: the way we live prompts certain genes to express themselves differently. Ana admits that, with two pregnancies behind her, she wonders whether something could have developed in the meantime, because during preparation for pregnancy she did not check her insulin status.

sections.subtitle: OGTT, metformin i biljne molekule: kako provjeriti i podržati inzulin
sections.screenshot_description: Gošća objašnjava kako izgleda OGTT test i mjerenje inzulina u tri točke
sections.content:
Mirna Sentić savjetuje da se inzulin provjeri uvijek. Pravom pretragom, za koju kaže da će se s njom složiti svi endokrinolozi, smatra **OGTT**, oralni test opterećenja glukozom:

- glukoza se mjeri natašte, 60 minuta i 120 minuta nakon što se popije čaša otopljenog šećera,
- u istim se trima točkama mjeri i inzulin,
- tek tako se pravilno procjenjuje inzulinska osjetljivost, odnosno rezistencija.

Na temelju nalaza endokrinolog odlučuje je li potrebna terapija. Gošća spominje **metformin**, lijek koji pomaže da glukoza lakše uđe u stanice i rasterećuje krv od viška inzulina. Taj je višak, objašnjava, važan jer inzulin koji ostane u krvotoku traži novu glukozu. Zato se javljaju čežnje i žudnje za hranom. Metformin, ističe Mirna, učinkovito djeluje već 60 godina, ali nije za svakoga.

U okviru nutricionizma postoje i druge mogućnosti: **mioinozitoli i berberin**. Riječ je o molekulama iz biljnog svijeta, sintetiziranima, koje mogu pomoći da stanica postane osjetljivija i bolje prima glukozu. Kada Ana pita ulazi li se time u svijet suplemenata, Mirna odgovara da je najvažnije na vrijeme otkriti i riješiti slabiju inzulinsku osjetljivost ili hiperinzulinemiju. Inzulinsku rezistenciju opisuje kao kišobran pod kojim se nalaze različite nijanse istog problema. Ženama s policističnim sindromom, inzulinskom rezistencijom ili teškoćama sa začećem poručuje: **obavezno provjeriti inzulin**. Jajnici ne moraju izgledati policistično da bi žena imala sindrom.
sections.subtitle_en: OGTT, Metformin, and Plant Molecules: How to Check and Support Insulin
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest explains what the OGTT test and three-point insulin measurement look like
sections.content_en:
Mirna Sentić advises that insulin should always be checked. As the proper test, with which she says all endocrinologists will agree, she considers the **OGTT**, the oral glucose tolerance test:

- glucose is measured fasting, 60 minutes, and 120 minutes after drinking a glass of dissolved sugar,
- insulin is measured at the same three points,
- only in this way can insulin sensitivity, that is, resistance, be properly evaluated.

Based on the findings, the endocrinologist decides whether therapy is needed. The guest mentions **metformin**, a drug that helps glucose enter cells more easily and relieves the blood of excess insulin. That excess, she explains, is important because insulin remaining in the bloodstream looks for new glucose. That is why cravings and food yearnings occur. Metformin, Mirna emphasizes, has worked effectively for 60 years, but it is not for everyone.

Within the scope of nutrition, other possibilities also exist: **myo-inositols and berberine**. These are molecules from the plant world, synthesized, that can help the cell become more sensitive and receive glucose better. When Ana asks whether this enters the world of supplements, Mirna replies that the most important thing is to detect and resolve lower insulin sensitivity or hyperinsulinemia in time. She describes insulin resistance as an umbrella under which different shades of the same problem are found. To women with polycystic syndrome, insulin resistance, or difficulties conceiving, she says: **make sure to check insulin**. Ovaries do not have to look polycystic for a woman to have the syndrome.

sections.subtitle: Hormonska hijerarhija: kad nije sve posloženo, nema reprodukcije
sections.screenshot_description: Mirna Sentić izgovara misao da roditeljstvo kreće od ideje, a ne od pozitivnog testa
sections.content:
Mirna Sentić objašnjava da problem može biti i na razini **štitnjače** s neodgovarajućim TSH-om, na razini **nadbubrežnih žlijezda** (kortizol, adrenalin) ili na razini **gušterače** kod hiperinzulinemije. Reproduktivni hormoni dolaze tek nakon toga. „Tako je to priroda osmislila. Ako nije sve posloženo, nema reprodukcije“, kaže gošća.

Prema njezinim riječima žena nije reproduktivno sposobna ni kada stres dolazi izvana. Kao primjer navodi zakonitosti prirode: nakon požara šuma se sama obnavlja, a u ratu nitko nije u „fertility modu“, ali nakon njega slijedi baby boom. Ista se logika, kaže, vidi i u svakodnevici. Želja za drugim djetetom najčešće se rađa iz obilja i stabilnosti, u zdravom odnosu i kada je ženi lijepo.

Gošća spominje i vlastitu obitelj. Njezina majka ima šestero djece i uvijek je imala velike odgovornosti u korporacijama. Znala joj je reći: „S tobom sam kozliće prodavala i ne možeš bit nego takva.“ Mirna duboko vjeruje da žene dio svojih sposobnosti prenose na djecu. Začeće nije samo čin, nego i neka vrsta „kodiranja“, trenutna snimka oba partnera koja se odražava u novom životu.

Iz toga proizlazi misao koju je Ana Pavlović odmah izdvojila kao isječak: **„Roditeljstvo kreće od ideje. Od ideje da vi i partner budete roditelji.“** Ne počinje kada se ugleda plus na testu ni kada beba zaplače, jer to je već ostvarenje. Počinje njegovanjem ideje i vrijednosti s kojima će se dijete kasnije odgajati. Ana dodaje da ta ideja dolazi vrlo rano jer djevojčice o tome maštaju, a Mirna to naziva majčinskim instinktom.
sections.subtitle_en: Hormonal Hierarchy: When Everything Is Not Aligned, There Is No Reproduction
sections.screenshot_description_en: Mirna Sentić utters the thought that parenthood starts from an idea, not from a positive test
sections.content_en:
Mirna Sentić explains that the problem can also be at the level of the **thyroid** with inappropriate TSH, at the level of the **adrenal glands** (cortisol, adrenaline), or at the level of the **pancreas** in hyperinsulinemia. Reproductive hormones come only after that. „That is how nature designed it. If everything is not aligned, there is no reproduction,“ says the guest.

According to her words, a woman is not reproductively capable even when stress comes from the outside. As an example, she cites the laws of nature: after a fire the forest renews itself, and in wartime no one is in „fertility mode,“ but after it comes a baby boom. The same logic, she says, is seen in everyday life. The desire for a second child is most often born out of abundance and stability, in a healthy relationship and when things are nice for the woman.

The guest also mentions her own family. Her mother has six children and always had great responsibilities in corporations. She used to tell her: „I sold baby goats with you and you can't be anything but like this.“ Mirna deeply believes that women pass on part of their abilities to their children. Conception is not merely an act, but also a kind of „coding,“ a momentary snapshot of both partners that is reflected in the new life.

From this comes the thought that Ana Pavlović immediately highlighted as a clip: **„Parenthood starts from an idea. From the idea that you and your partner will be parents.“** It does not begin when a plus is seen on a test nor when the baby cries, because that is already fulfillment. It begins by nurturing the idea and the values with which the child will later be raised. Ana adds that this idea comes very early because little girls dream about it, and Mirna calls that maternal instinct.

sections.subtitle: Mršavi ili debeli tip? Zašto etikete ne pomažu
sections.screenshot_description: Gošća objašnjava zašto joj se ne sviđa podjela na mršavi i debeli tip PCOS-a
sections.content:
Ana Pavlović vraća razgovor na simptome. Pita prepoznaje li se sindrom nužno po višku kilograma, aknama ili pojačanoj dlakavosti. Prisjeća se da su se iz srednje škole i s fakulteta upravo ti simptomi povezivali s dijagnozom kod njezinih prijateljica.

„Apsolutno ne“, odgovara Mirna Sentić. Hiperinzulinemiju može imati i žena vrlo mršavog fenotipa, kako se to naziva u medicinskoj literaturi. Gošća otvoreno kaže da se naježi kada vidi klasifikaciju na „mršavi“ i „debeli“ tip PCOS-a. Ne slaže se ni s nazivom „androgeni tip“. Smatra da ženi treba objasniti u kojem se dijelu hormonske slagalice nalazi problem. Sumnja na PMOS zbog viška kilograma, povećanog BMI-ja, dlakavosti ili anovulacije opravdana je, ali tada treba napraviti probir i otkriti „odakle vjetar puše“:

- **probir štitnjače**,
- **probir gušterače**, za koji nije nužan OGTT jer se može izračunati **HOMA indeks**, odnos inzulina i glukoze izmjerenih natašte,
- **razgovor o navikama**, jer žena možda upravo njima pojačava nešto što je u njoj genetski zapisano.

Tek nakon analiza i uvida u način života, ističe Mirna, može se savjetovati i nešto upisati u nalaz. Razumije da je liječnicima podjela na tipove praktična u dijagnostici, ali smatra da je „PCOS žena puno više“ od toga. Spominje kolegicu **Luciju Paulu**, koja je također gostovala u podcastu i koja joj je pomogla bolje razumjeti PCOS. Žene sa sindromom često se opisuju kao hiperosjetljive. Mirna to objašnjava stalnim viškom nekog hormona: prolaktina, kortizola, inzulina, nadbubrežnih ili muških spolnih hormona. Ti viškovi, prema njezinu tumačenju, nastaju jer negdje „senzori bolje rade“.
sections.subtitle_en: Lean or Fat Type? Why Labels Do Not Help
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest explains why she does not like the division into lean and fat types of PCOS
sections.content_en:
Ana Pavlović returns the conversation to symptoms. She asks whether the syndrome is necessarily recognized by excess weight, acne, or increased body hair. She recalls that from high school and college, precisely those symptoms were associated with the diagnosis among her friends.

„Absolutely not,“ replies Mirna Sentić. A woman with a very lean phenotype, as it is called in medical literature, can also have hyperinsulinemia. The guest openly says that she cringes when she sees the classification into „lean“ and „fat“ types of PCOS. Nor does she agree with the name „androgenic type.“ She believes that it should be explained to the woman in which part of the hormonal puzzle the problem lies. Suspicion of PMOS due to excess weight, increased BMI, hirsutism, or anovulation is justified, but then screening should be done to find out „which way the wind is blowing“:

- **thyroid screening**,
- **pancreas screening**, for which an OGTT is not necessary because the **HOMA index** can be calculated, the ratio of fasting measured insulin and glucose,
- **a conversation about habits**, because through them a woman might be amplifying something that is genetically written in her.

Only after analyses and insight into lifestyle, Mirna emphasizes, can advice be given and something entered into the medical record. She understands that the division into types is practical for doctors in diagnostics, but believes that „the PCOS woman is much more“ than that. She mentions colleague **Lucija Paula**, who was also a guest on the podcast and who helped her better understand PCOS. Women with the syndrome are often described as hypersensitive. Mirna explains this by a constant excess of some hormone: prolactin, cortisol, insulin, adrenal, or male sex hormones. Those excesses, according to her interpretation, occur because somewhere „sensors work better.“

sections.subtitle: PCOS žene kao ratnice: evolucijsko tumačenje sindroma
sections.screenshot_description: Mirna Sentić opisuje evolucijsku teoriju o PCOS ženama kao čuvaricama legla
sections.content:
Mirna Sentić svoje klijentice s PCOS-om rado naziva **ratnicama**. Tijekom sedam do osam godina vlastitog istraživanja, prije nego što je odlučila potpuno se posvetiti ovom području, naišla je na tumačenje da je sindrom nastao evolucijski.

Prema toj teoriji, dok su plodne žene bile zaštićene u leglu, a muškarci odlazili u lov, postojale su i žene koje su čuvale zajednicu. Gošća objašnjava kako bi svaki „višak“ toj ženi bio prednost:

- **višak kortizola** omogućuje joj da ostane budna noću,
- **višak inzulina** omogućuje joj da dulje izdrži bez hrane,
- **višak testosterona** daje joj veću mišićnu masu.

Takva žena može stalno biti u stanju „bori se ili bježi“, ali zbog toga nije uvijek plodna. „To joj je danak. Čuva leglo, to je njezina svrha“, kaže Mirna. Opisuje je kao izvrsnu organizatoricu s dobrim menadžerskim vještinama. Da bi ušla u reproduktivnu fazu, mora snažno smiriti vanjske stresore i podražaje kako ne bi stalno bila na oprezu.

Gošća ističe da ovu priču rado prepričava ženama. Kada žena dođe osuđena „iz sustava“ i traži odgovore, a uvjerena je da s njom nešto ne valja, da nikada neće ostati trudna, da ne može uhvatiti ovulaciju i da mora na stimulacije, ne može vidjeti ni čuti sljedeći korak. Zato Mirna zagovara pristup bez obeshrabrivanja, s jasnim imenovanjem problema.
sections.subtitle_en: PCOS Women as Warriors: An Evolutionary Interpretation of the Syndrome
sections.screenshot_description_en: Mirna Sentić describes the evolutionary theory of PCOS women as guardians of the brood
sections.content_en:
Mirna Sentić gladly refers to her clients with PCOS as **warriors**. During seven to eight years of her own research, before deciding to dedicate herself entirely to this field, she came across the interpretation that the syndrome originated evolutionarily.

According to that theory, while fertile women were protected in the brood and men went out to hunt, there were also women who guarded the community. The guest explains how every „excess“ would be an advantage for that woman:

- **excess cortisol** allows her to stay awake at night,
- **excess insulin** allows her to endure longer without food,
- **excess testosterone** gives her greater muscle mass.

Such a woman can constantly be in a state of „fight or flight,“ but because of that she is not always fertile. „That is her toll. She guards the brood, that is her purpose,“ says Mirna. She describes her as an excellent organizer with good managerial skills. In order to enter the reproductive phase, she must strongly calm external stressors and stimuli so as not to be constantly on alert.

The guest emphasizes that she gladly retells this story to women. When a woman arrives judged „by the system“ and searches for answers, convinced that something is wrong with her, that she will never get pregnant, that she cannot catch ovulation, and that she has to undergo stimulations, she cannot see or hear the next step. Therefore, Mirna advocates an approach without discouragement, with clearly naming the problem.

sections.subtitle: „U svijetu AI-a, biram ljudski pristup“: humane klinike bez posramljivanja
sections.screenshot_description: Gošća poručuje da klinike za humanu reprodukciju trebaju biti humane
sections.content:
Iz priče o ratnicama Mirna Sentić izvodi jednu od najsnažnijih poruka epizode: **„U svijetu AI-a, ja biram ljudski pristup.“** I sama je predložila da se ta rečenica izdvoji kao isječak.

Smatra da takav mora biti cijeli pristup plodnosti, a da klinike za humanu reprodukciju moraju biti **humane**, s ljudima koji pomažu doći do bebe ako je to izbor para. Navodi da netko nema drugog izbora, primjerice žena bez jajovoda. Takve odluke treba poštovati i kroz njih prolaziti s ljudskošću, a ne s osudom i pitanjima poput „Što si čekala do sada?“. Žene su, kaže, možda čekale partnera ili dobre uvjete.

„Nema posramljivanja“, naglašava gošća. Uvjerena je da svaki put kada se jedna žena posrami, druga postane još odlučnija upozoriti ostale. Plodnost opisuje kao dar i podsjeća na riječi „blagoslovljena ti među ženama“: žena je blagoslovljena kada je plodna, i bilo bi dobro kada bi se plodnost tretirala kao nešto sveto.
sections.subtitle_en: „In a World of AI, I Choose the Human Approach“: Humane Clinics Without Shaming
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest says that clinics for human reproduction should be humane
sections.content_en:
From the story of the warriors, Mirna Sentić derives one of the strongest messages of the episode: **„In a world of AI, I choose the human approach.“** She herself suggested that this sentence be singled out as a clip.

She believes that the entire approach to fertility must be like that, and that clinics for human reproduction must be **humane**, with people who help bring about a baby if that is the couple's choice. She states that someone has no other choice, for example a woman without fallopian tubes. Such decisions should be respected and navigated with humanity, not with judgment and questions like „What have you been waiting for until now?“. Women, she says, may have been waiting for a partner or good conditions.

„There is no shaming,“ emphasizes the guest. She is convinced that every time one woman is shamed, another becomes even more determined to warn the rest. She describes fertility as a gift and recalls the words „blessed art thou among women“: a woman is blessed when she is fertile, and it would be good if fertility were treated as something sacred.

sections.subtitle: Ništa bez muškaraca: „Jača si od mene, ali ja sam ti stabilniji“
sections.screenshot_description: Mirna Sentić prepričava razgovor sa suprugom o snazi i stabilnosti
sections.content:
Ana Pavlović priznaje da ponekad poželi biti muškarac jer bi joj život bio lakši i manje bi se stresirala. Odmah dodaje da bi tada i manje doživljavala svijet. Uz šaljivo „no offense“ kamermanima kaže da je ženski unutarnji svijet puno bogatiji. To bogatstvo zna opteretiti, ali ga nadoknađuje spoznaja da žena može nositi drugo tijelo u sebi i dati mu život. Naravno, dodaje, „bez njih ništa“.

Mirna Sentić se slaže i podsjeća na izreku „muž izgradi kuću, žena napravi dom“. Muškarac je, kaže, tu da stvara i pruža stabilnost. Prepričava razgovor sa suprugom nakon jednog lošeg dana, kada mu je rekla da je mislila kako je jaka, a da se osjeća nestabilno. On joj je odgovorio: **„Jesi ti jaka. Jača si od mene, ali ja sam ti stabilniji.“** Gošća to naziva istinom koju rado citira.

Odnos opisuje slikovito: žene su sinusoide, a muškarci ravna crta koja prolazi kroz njih. Bez te stabilnosti, kaže, žene „nemaju smisla“. Zaključuje: **„Bez njih ništa. S njima sve.“** Ana dodaje da u lijepom partnerskom odnosu, punom sigurnosti i bez osude, žena može otvoreno i bez grča krenuti prema plodnosti i trudnoći. Upozorava da i u stabilnim odnosima i uz podršku okoline kroz glavu prolaze misli poput „ne valjam“, „to neću moći“ i „do mene je“. Takve misli same po sebi dižu kortizol.
sections.subtitle_en: Nothing Without Men: „You Are Stronger Than Me, but I Am More Stable Than You“
sections.screenshot_description_en: Mirna Sentić retells a conversation with her husband about strength and stability
sections.content_en:
Ana Pavlović admits that sometimes she wishes she were a man because life would be easier for her and she would stress less. She immediately adds that then she would also experience the world less. With a playful „no offense“ to the cameramen, she says that a woman's inner world is much richer. That richness can be burdensome, but it is compensated by the realization that a woman can carry another body inside herself and give it life. Of course, she adds, „nothing without them.“

Mirna Sentić agrees and recalls the saying „a husband builds a house, a wife makes a home.“ A man is there, she says, to create and provide stability. She retells a conversation with her husband after a bad day, when she told him she thought she was strong, but that she felt unstable. He replied to her: **„You are strong. You are stronger than me, but I am more stable than you.“** The guest calls that a truth she gladly quotes.

She describes the relationship vividly: women are sine waves, and men are the straight line passing through them. Without that stability, she says, women „make no sense.“ She concludes: **„Without them, nothing. With them, everything.“** Ana adds that in a lovely partnership, full of security and without judgment, a woman can openly and without tension move toward fertility and pregnancy. She warns that even in stable relationships and with support from one's surroundings, thoughts like „I am no good,“ „I won't be able to do this,“ and „it's on me“ run through one's head. Such thoughts raise cortisol on their own.

sections.subtitle: Plodnost kao test partnerstva: fifty-fifty i bez traženja krivca
sections.screenshot_description: Gošća poručuje parovima da su obitelj i bez djece
sections.content:
Mirna Sentić primjećuje da sve više parova dolazi zajedno. Muškarci su, kaže, „tu za nas“. Smatra da su žene generacije milenijalaca, koja čini većinu publike podcasta, prekinule transgeneracijske obrasce i dopustile partnerima da sudjeluju. Napominje da je to njezino osobno uvjerenje.

Kada par kaže „Mi imamo problem“, ne smije se tražiti krivac jer je **ulog pedeset-pedeset**. „Kemija, priroda i Bog su tu da kažu: vrijeme je, i sad je“, kaže gošća. Na partnerima je da se svaki dan pitaju kako mogu pomoći jedno drugome. Zato teškoće sa začećem vidi kao **test partnerstva**: koliko su dvoje ljudi dobri partneri i dobra obitelj.

Posebno naglašava da je par **obitelj i bez djece**, jer su jedno drugo izabrali pred Bogom. Lijepo je kada se može dati plod, ali to nije nužno da bi se potvrdili partnerstvo i obitelj. Poziva i da se ne sudi ni partneru ni liječniku. Previše vremena odlazi na ljutnju i krivnju, emocije koje „ukorjenjuju“. Tuga, bol i ljutnja normalan su dio života i smiju se osjetiti, ali ne smiju okovati ženu. Srce spremno za majčinstvo je otvoreno, ono prima i daje. Potrebno je vrijeme da žena prijeđe iz stanja „tužna sam, ljuta sam, zašto ne ja“ u stanje „prihvaćam, radim i vjerujem da dolazi pravi trenutak za mene“.

Ana Pavlović potvrđuje da se često čuje kako je trudnoća došla upravo kada je žena bila najmanje opterećena. Mirna to naziva prepuštanjem. Obje zaključuju da „glava jako puno radi“ i da su, krenuvši od hormona, došle do svrhe. Gošća sažima: hormoni su naše emocije i emotivna stanja, a definiraju nas i ljudi kojima se okružujemo.
sections.subtitle_en: Fertility as a Test of Partnership: Fifty-Fifty and Without Looking for Someone to Blame
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest tells couples that they are a family even without children
sections.content_en:
Mirna Sentić notes that more and more couples are coming together. Men are, she says, „there for us.“ She believes that women of the millennial generation, who make up the majority of the podcast audience, have broken transgenerational patterns and allowed partners to participate. She notes that this is her personal belief.

When a couple says „We have a problem,“ one must not look for someone to blame because the **stake is fifty-fifty**. „Chemistry, nature, and God are there to say: it is time, and now is the time,“ says the guest. It is up to the partners to ask each other every day how they can help one another. That is why she sees difficulties conceiving as a **test of partnership**: how good of partners and how good of a family two people are.

She particularly emphasizes that a couple is a **family even without children**, because they chose each other before God. It is lovely when fruit can be given, but that is not necessary to validate partnership and family. She also urges not to judge either partner or doctor. Too much time is spent on anger and guilt, emotions that „take root.“ Sadness, pain, and anger are a normal part of life and are allowed to be felt, but they must not shackle a woman. A heart ready for motherhood is open; it receives and gives. It takes time for a woman to transition from the state of „I am sad, I am angry, why not me“ to the state of „I accept, I work, and I believe that the right moment is coming for me.“

Ana Pavlović confirms that one often hears how pregnancy came precisely when the woman was least burdened. Mirna calls that surrender. Both conclude that „the head works very hard“ and that, starting from hormones, they have arrived at purpose. The guest summarizes: hormones are our emotions and emotional states, and we are also defined by the people we surround ourselves with.

sections.subtitle: Meso ili ugljikohidrati? Što otkrivaju žudnje u PMS-u
sections.screenshot_description: Voditeljica i gošća uspoređuju što žude u PMS-u, meso ili ugljikohidrate
sections.content:
Na pitanje smiju li se žene izvlačiti na hormone, Mirna Sentić kroz smijeh odgovara potvrdno i priznaje da je upravo u PMS-u. Ana Pavlović otkriva da je gošća na ručku prije snimanja tražila meso, a ona sama u PMS-u uvijek žudi za ugljikohidratima. Mirna kaže da su obje reakcije smislene.

Žudnju za mesom gošća u svom tumačenju povezuje s pripremom tijela za gubitak krvi i potrebom za željezom. Moguće je i da je u lutealnoj fazi slabije osjetljiva na inzulin. Kada u toj fazi pada progesteron, tijelo dobiva signal da nema ploda i priprema se za krvarenje.

Žudnju za slatkim i ugljikohidratima objašnjava time što je početak trudnoće hormonski sličan PMS-u. Tijelo ne zna je li začeće nastupilo, pa smanjuje osjetljivost na inzulin i stvara zalihe energije za mogući novi život. Zato se ženama u PMS-u jede slatko jer energetski „nemaju pojma gdje su“. Kada progesteron naglo padne i endometrij se oljušti, tijelo kao da kaže: „Evo me, prokrvarila sam, dobra sam, stabilna.“
sections.subtitle_en: Meat or Carbohydrates? What Cravings Reveal in PMS
sections.screenshot_description_en: Host and guest compare what they crave in PMS, meat or carbohydrates
sections.content_en:
To the question of whether women are allowed to make excuses with hormones, Mirna Sentić responds affirmatively through laughter and admits that she is currently in PMS. Ana Pavlović reveals that the guest asked for meat at lunch before the recording, while she herself always craves carbohydrates during PMS. Mirna says that both reactions make sense.

The craving for meat the guest connects in her interpretation with the body's preparation for blood loss and the need for iron. It is also possible that she is less sensitive to insulin in the luteal phase. When progesterone drops in that phase, the body receives a signal that there is no fruit and prepares for bleeding.

She explains the craving for sweets and carbohydrates by the fact that the beginning of pregnancy is hormonally similar to PMS. The body does not know whether conception has occurred, so it reduces insulin sensitivity and builds up energy reserves for possible new life. That is why women in PMS feel like eating sweets because energetically „they have no idea where they are.“ When progesterone drops sharply and the endometrium sheds, the body seems to say: „Here I am, I've started bleeding, I'm good, stable.“

sections.subtitle: Žuto tijelo, progesteron i kortizol: zašto je PMS nekad jači
sections.screenshot_description: Mirna Sentić objašnjava ulogu žutog tijela i progesterona u jačini PMS-a
sections.content:
Kada Ana Pavlović pita imaju li jači simptomi PMS-a veze s inzulinom, Mirna Sentić potvrđuje, ali dodaje i drugi čimbenik: **snagu žutog tijela**. Opisuje ga kao „ožiljak“ koji ostaje na mjestu folikula iz kojeg se dogodila ovulacija. Napominje da je riječ o ginekološkom pitanju i da surađuje s ginekologinjama, **doktoricom Petrom Kejlom** i **doktoricom Petrom Kojandom**, koje naziva svojim mentoricama.

Snaga žutog tijela s godinama slabi. Progesteron postaje nestabilniji, a mogu se javiti probojna i točkasta krvarenja u lutealnoj fazi. Nakon 35. godine ciklus, kako kaže gošća, „otkriva“ da je žena manje plodna. Što je progesteron nestabilniji, to je PMS izraženiji. Stres to dodatno pogoršava: kada se žena naljuti ili je pod pritiskom, **kortizol „krade“ receptore progesteronu**, pa su simptomi još jači.

Prvu fazu ciklusa Mirna naziva **proljećem**. Tada žene štiti estrogen, koji djeluje kao filter. Zato žene u menopauzi, kada estrogen nestane, kažu da su „svoje odradile“ jer, prema riječima gošće, više nemaju cenzuru. Estrogen za ženu opisuje kao ekvivalent testosteronu, izvor stabilnosti do ovulacije. Ovulaciju naziva darom i drugom frekvencijom. Jedna njezina klijentica, operna pjevačica, govorila joj je da određenu dionicu može otpjevati bez pucanja glasa samo ako je pjeva u vrijeme ovulacije.

Nakon toga dolazi progesteronska faza. Tada bi žene, prema Mirninu savjetu, trebale usporiti, paziti na inzulin i jesti više proteina. Kolač je dopušten, ali „poljubljen uz obrok“, a ne samostalno, jer bi bez proteina, odnosno „cjepanice“, žudnja trajala cijeli dan.
sections.subtitle_en: Corpus Luteum, Progesterone, and Cortisol: Why PMS Is Sometimes Stronger
sections.screenshot_description_en: Mirna Sentić explains the role of the corpus luteum and progesterone in the severity of PMS
sections.content_en:
When Ana Pavlović asks whether stronger PMS symptoms have something to do with insulin, Mirna Sentić confirms, but also adds a second factor: the **strength of the corpus luteum**. She describes it as a „scar“ that remains at the site of the follicle from which ovulation occurred. She notes that this is a gynecological question and that she collaborates with gynecologists, **Dr. Petra Kejla** and **Dr. Petra Kojanda**, whom she calls her mentors.

The strength of the corpus luteum weakens with age. Progesterone becomes more unstable, and breakthrough and spotting bleeding may occur in the luteal phase. After age 35, the cycle, as the guest says, „reveals“ that a woman is less fertile. The more unstable the progesterone is, the more pronounced the PMS. Stress worsens this further: when a woman gets angry or is under pressure, **cortisol „steals“ receptors from progesterone**, making the symptoms even stronger.

Mirna calls the first phase of the cycle **spring**. Then women are protected by estrogen, which acts like a filter. That is why women in menopause, when estrogen disappears, say that they have „done their part“ because, in the guest's words, they no longer have a filter. She describes estrogen for a woman as the equivalent of testosterone, a source of stability until ovulation. She calls ovulation a gift and a different frequency. One of her clients, an opera singer, told her that she could sing a certain passage without her voice cracking only if she sang it at the time of ovulation.

After that comes the progesterone phase. Then women should, according to Mirna's advice, slow down, watch their insulin, and eat more protein. Cake is allowed, but „kissed with a meal,“ not on its own, because without protein, that is, the „log,“ the craving would last all day.

sections.subtitle: Čokolada bez krivnje i „sretne kalorije“ na putovanju
sections.screenshot_description: Gošća prepričava kako joj je prijatelj Mislav citirao rečenicu o sretnim kalorijama
sections.content:
Ana Pavlović opisuje poznatu situaciju: žena u PMS-u pojede cijelu čokoladu i potom osjeća krivnju. Dodaje da cijela čokolada vjerojatno ne bi ni bila pojedena da je prije toga bilo dobrog obroka.

Mirna Sentić ne voli osjećaj krivnje oko hrane. Ako je čokolada pojedena, dovoljno je reći „uživala sam“, bez samooptuživanja tipa „što mi je ovo trebalo“. Pomaže i jednostavno „neka sam“. Iako je nutricionistica, gošća poručuje da je bolje osjetiti ponos i snagu nego krivnju, jer tijelo na to **puno bolje hormonski reagira**.

Tu misao ilustrira pričom o **Mislavu**, kojeg opisuje kao rođaka, prijatelja i srodnu dušu. Mislav joj je rekao da je se uvijek sjeti kada jede na putovanju. Ona mu je, naime, jednom rekla da **„na putovanju postoje samo sretne kalorije“**. On rado putuje u Italiju, a hranu je ondje jeo u dobrom društvu i s osmijehom, pa se vraćao lakši iako je ta hrana bila glikemijski zahtjevna. Gošća tvrdi da je to znanstveno dokazano: kada je čovjek u dobrom društvu, smije se uz obrok i osjeća zadovoljstvo, cijelo tijelo i hormoni mu žele pomoći. Naravno, ne treba pretjerivati, ali ako se guštalo, nema mjesta krivnji.
sections.subtitle_en: Chocolate Without Guilt and „Happy Calories“ on a Trip
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest retells how her friend Mislav quoted her sentence about happy calories
sections.content_en:
Ana Pavlović describes a familiar situation: a woman in PMS eats an entire chocolate bar and then feels guilty. She adds that an entire chocolate bar probably would not have been eaten at all if there had been a good meal beforehand.

Mirna Sentić does not like feelings of guilt around food. If the chocolate was eaten, it is enough to say „I enjoyed it,“ without self-blame like „why did I need this.“ A simple „good for me“ also helps. Although she is a nutritionist, the guest says that it is better to feel pride and strength than guilt, because the body **hormonally reacts much better** to that.

She illustrates that thought with a story about **Mislav**, whom she describes as a cousin, friend, and soulmate. Mislav told her that he always remembers her when he eats while traveling. Namely, she once told him that **„on a trip there are only happy calories“**. He gladly travels to Italy, and he ate food there in good company and with a smile, returning lighter even though that food was glycemically demanding. The guest claims that this is scientifically proven: when a person is in good company, laughs over a meal, and feels pleasure, the whole body and hormones want to help him. Of course, one should not overdo it, but if it was relished, there is no place for guilt.

sections.subtitle: Balans bez ortoreksije: trećina, četvrtina, šestina i noćni post
sections.screenshot_description: Mirna Sentić objašnjava raspodjelu ugljikohidrata kroz dan i važnost noćnog posta
sections.content:
Ana Pavlović traži recept za ravnotežu: paziti što se jede, a ne oduzeti si svaki užitak. Mirna Sentić upozorava da s druge strane postoji spektar **ortoreksije**, bolesnog odnosa prema hrani s neprestanim mjerenjem i vaganjem. Zato je važno odrediti cilj i prilagoditi mu prehranu.

Smisao balansirane prehrane gošća sažima ovako: jesti tako da hrana koristi, da se iz nje dobiju nutrijenti i energija za sve fizičke aktivnosti, da nema umora tijekom dana i da se kvalitetno spava. Put do toga je tanjur podijeljen na trećine uz proteinsku „cjepanicu“.

Za one koji žele smršavjeti ključ je pametno raspoređivanje ugljikohidrata:

- **doručak**: ugljikohidrati čine trećinu tanjura,
- **ručak**: četvrtinu tanjura,
- **večera**: šestinu tanjura ili ih uopće nema.

Objašnjava da je inzulin hormon koji donosi energiju i sitost, i da i on mora „spavati“ dio noći. Mršavi se upravo noću, pa je **noćni post** normalan. Post tijekom dana je moguć, ali tada sve radi sporije, uključujući mozak, jer nema brzo dostupne energije. Važno je poštovati porcije, ponavljati obrasce i pustiti tijelo da preko noći ogladni i potraži energiju iz zaliha. Bez takvih uvjeta, ističe gošća, nema ni mršavljenja. Spominje i bazalni metabolizam, potrošnju u mirovanju, koju tjelesna aktivnost može povećati za 200, 300 do 500 kalorija. Upozorava da se to „lako pojede“.
sections.subtitle_en: Balance without orthorexia: a third, a quarter, a sixth, and overnight fasting
sections.screenshot_description_en: Mirna Sentić explains the distribution of carbohydrates throughout the day and the importance of overnight fasting
sections.content_en:
Ana Pavlović is looking for a recipe for balance: paying attention to what one eats, without depriving oneself of every pleasure. Mirna Sentić warns that on the other side exists the spectrum of **orthorexia**, an unhealthy relationship with food with constant measuring and weighing. That is why it is important to determine a goal and adapt nutrition to it.

The guest summarizes the meaning of a balanced diet like this: eating in such a way that food benefits you, that nutrients and energy for all physical activities are obtained from it, that there is no fatigue during the day, and that one sleeps well. The path to that is a plate divided into thirds alongside a protein "log".

For those who want to lose weight, the key is the smart distribution of carbohydrates:

- **breakfast**: carbohydrates make up a third of the plate,
- **lunch**: a quarter of the plate,
- **dinner**: a sixth of the plate or none at all.

She explains that insulin is a hormone that brings energy and satiety, and that it too must "sleep" part of the night. Weight loss happens precisely at night, so **overnight fasting** is normal. Fasting during the day is possible, but then everything works more slowly, including the brain, because there is no readily available energy. It is important to respect portions, repeat patterns, and let the body get hungry overnight and seek energy from reserves. Without such conditions, points out the guest, there is no weight loss either. She also mentions basal metabolism, resting energy expenditure, which physical activity can increase by 200, 300 up to 500 calories. She warns that this is "easily eaten away".

sections.subtitle: „Pojedi da se ne baci“: ostaci dječje hrane i balkanska kultura obilja
sections.screenshot_description: Voditeljica i gošća razgovaraju o ostacima dječje hrane i kulturi obilja
sections.content:
Ana Pavlović prepričava objavu jedne majke koja je cijeli dan fotografirala što je pojela za svojom djecom: pola Kinder čokoladice, pola jabuke, trećinu banane. Samo od ostataka skupila je 600 do 700 kalorija. Ana dodaje da to vjerojatno rade sve majke.

Mirna Sentić napominje da svakodnevno kretanje, pješačenje ili vožnja biciklom mogu nadoknaditi takve „guštove“. Kada Ana kaže da to nije gušt nego potreba da se hrana ne baci, gošća otvara širu temu. Govori o **balkanskoj kulturi hranjenja**, koju naziva kulturom obilja: „Nama nemoj da fali.“ Spominje i izreke koje to njeguju, poput „uzmi da se ne baci“ i „gladne su mi oči“. Ana dodaje da je ta navika nastala iz neimaštine koju su prijašnje generacije prolazile, a Mirna se slaže.

Gošća primjećuje da nitko nije učio kako jesti koliko je potrebno i umjereno. Sitost je bila simbol sigurnosti. Šaljivo priznaje da joj je hladnjak pun ostataka. Suprug je zna pitati otkad stoje, a ona ih čuva u nadi da će ih dodati u dječju kašu. Savjetuje da se ostaci radije spreme u hladnjak ili daju životinjama, ali uz svijest o tome što se radi. Balans, kaže, počinje od svakodnevnih uvjerenja i svijesti o tome što želimo.

Njezin je cilj tijelo koje služi: da se može popeti na planinu, potrčati za djetetom ili busom i zavezati vezice bez muke. „Mi smo stvoreni za pokret“, poručuje gošća. Priroda ima samo jedan način potrošnje energije, a to je kretanje. Ljudi su pak, dodaje, smislili način kako zamaskirati prirodnu glad.
sections.subtitle_en: "Eat it so it doesn't go to waste": children's food leftovers and the Balkan culture of abundance
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host and the guest discuss children's food leftovers and the culture of abundance
sections.content_en:
Ana Pavlović recounts a post by a mother who photographed what she ate after her children all day long: half a Kinder chocolate bar, half an apple, a third of a banana. From leftovers alone she accumulated 600 to 700 calories. Ana adds that probably all mothers do that.

Mirna Sentić notes that daily movement, walking, or riding a bicycle can compensate for such "treats". When Ana says that this is not a treat but a need not to waste food, the guest opens up a broader topic. She speaks about the **Balkan food culture**, which she calls a culture of abundance: "Let us not lack anything." She also mentions sayings that nurture this, such as "take it so it doesn't go to waste" and "my eyes are hungry". Ana adds that this habit arose from the poverty that previous generations went through, and Mirna agrees.

The guest observes that no one taught how to eat as much as needed and moderately. Fullness was a symbol of security. She jokingly admits that her refrigerator is full of leftovers. Her husband tends to ask how long they have been sitting there, and she saves them in hopes of adding them to baby porridge. She advises that leftovers should rather be stored in the refrigerator or given to animals, but with awareness of what one is doing. Balance, she says, starts from everyday beliefs and awareness of what we want.

Her goal is a body that serves: to be able to climb a mountain, run after a child or a bus, and tie shoelaces without struggle. "We are made for movement", says the guest. Nature has only one way of expending energy, and that is movement. People, however, she adds, have devised a way to mask natural hunger.

sections.subtitle: Nepravedno optužene namirnice: ugljikohidrati kao stvarna potreba
sections.screenshot_description: Mirna Sentić objašnjava zašto sportaši, trudnice, djeca i žene u PMS-u trebaju ugljikohidrate
sections.content:
Ana Pavlović podsjeća da su se njezini baka i djed kretali radeći u polju, dok se današnji način života promijenio. Uz te promjene stigle su i dijagnoze te izrazi kojima se olako razbacuje: gluten kao najveći krivac, intolerancija kod svake druge osobe, zabrana tjestenine i strah od kruha. Prijašnje nutricionistice u podcastu govorile su da je dio problema u pretjeranom unosu. Ana ipak smatra da si ljudi daju za pravo „optužiti“ i precrtati pojedine namirnice. Pita je li u redu jesti više ugljikohidrata u određenim životnim fazama, primjerice u određenoj fazi ciklusa, te je li voće problematično.

„Može, može, može“, odgovara Mirna Sentić. Ponavlja da se namirnica ne smije osuđivati bez poznavanja konteksta i nabraja primjere:

- **sportaš** bez ugljikohidrata sutradan ne može na teren, ne može obnoviti glikogen ni odraditi dva treninga,
- **trudnica** bi njihov izostanak jasno osjetila,
- osobama s **problemima želuca ili crijeva** njihovo izbacivanje nema smisla,
- **djeca** u rastu kada traže slatko zapravo traže visok inzulin, jer im omogućuje rast. Gošća predlaže da im se tada pripremi pura, griz ili tjestenina s nečim,
- **žena u PMS-u** je također u stvarnoj potrebi.

„Nije ovo excuse. Ovo je potreba“, zaključuje Mirna.
sections.subtitle_en: Unjustly accused foods: carbohydrates as a real need
sections.screenshot_description_en: Mirna Sentić explains why athletes, pregnant women, children, and women with PMS need carbohydrates
sections.content_en:
Ana Pavlović recalls that her grandmother and grandfather moved around working in the field, while today's lifestyle has changed. Along with these changes came diagnoses and terms thrown around lightly: gluten as the greatest culprit, intolerance in every other person, banning pasta, and fear of bread. Previous nutritionists on the podcast spoke about part of the problem being in excessive intake. Ana nevertheless believes that people give themselves the right to "accuse" and cross out certain foods. She asks whether it is okay to eat more carbohydrates in certain life phases, for example in a certain phase of the cycle, and whether fruit is problematic.

"Yes, yes, yes", answers Mirna Sentić. She reiterates that a food item must not be condemned without knowing the context and lists examples:

- an **athlete** without carbohydrates cannot take the field the next day, cannot replenish glycogen, nor complete two training sessions,
- a **pregnant woman** would clearly feel their absence,
- for people with **stomach or bowel issues**, eliminating them makes no sense,
- **growing children** when asking for sweets are actually asking for high insulin, because it enables them to grow. The guest suggests preparing polenta, semolina, or pasta with something for them then,
- a **woman with PMS** is also in real need.

"This is not an excuse. This is a need", concludes Mirna.

sections.subtitle: Gluten nije uzrok autoimunih bolesti
sections.screenshot_description: Gošća objašnjava razliku između celijakije, alergija i izbacivanja pekarskih proizvoda
sections.content:
Govoreći o glutenu, Mirna Sentić upozorava da su glutenski proizvodi većinom pekarski. Kada netko izbaci gluten, zapravo izbaci pekarske proizvode, pa je logično da smršavi. U tim proizvodima nema samo ugljikohidrata nego i puno masti: hrskavost dolazi upravo od masnoće, kao kod lisnatog tijesta.

Gluten je protein koji se, prema njezinim riječima, već 50-ak do 100 godina smatra problematičnim. Gošća ne umanjuje stvarne dijagnoze. Postoje **celijakija, alergija na gluten, alergija na pšenicu i intolerancije**, a sve se svrstavaju pod kišobran glutenske enteropatije. Važno je utvrditi gdje se pod tim kišobranom netko nalazi prije nego što počne izbacivati namirnice.

Kod osoba s autoimunim bolestima izbacivanje glutena sigurno će pomoći da crijevo bude mirnije. Crijevo je filter i mjesto komunikacije vanjskog i unutarnjeg svijeta, gdje nastaju i antitijela. No Mirna jasno poručuje da **gluten nije uzrok autoimune bolesti**. Ona nastaje iz kombinacije genetske podloge i načina života. Zato gošća ne voli savjete tipa „nemoj ovo, nemoj ono“, nego pita: „Zašto ti služi? Zašto ti treba?“
sections.subtitle_en: Gluten is not the cause of autoimmune diseases
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest explains the difference between celiac disease, allergies, and eliminating bakery products
sections.content_en:
Speaking about gluten, Mirna Sentić warns that gluten products are mostly bakery products. When someone eliminates gluten, they actually eliminate bakery products, so it is logical that they lose weight. In those products there are not only carbohydrates but also a lot of fat: crispiness comes precisely from fat, as with puff pastry.

Gluten is a protein that, according to her words, has been considered problematic for some 50 to 100 years. The guest does not diminish real diagnoses. There are **celiac disease, gluten allergy, wheat allergy, and intolerances**, and all fall under the umbrella of gluten enteropathy. It is important to determine where under that umbrella someone is before they begin eliminating foods.

In people with autoimmune diseases, eliminating gluten will certainly help the gut be calmer. The gut is a filter and a place of communication between the external and internal world, where antibodies are also created. But Mirna clearly conveys that **gluten is not the cause of autoimmune disease**. It arises from a combination of genetic background and lifestyle. That is why the guest does not like advice like "don't do this, don't do that", but asks: "What does it serve you for? Why do you need it?"

sections.subtitle: Al dente tjestenina i hladni krumpir: trikovi sa škrobom
sections.screenshot_description: Mirna Sentić objašnjava kako hlađenje krumpira i kuhanje al dente mijenjaju škrob
sections.content:
Mirnin stav o ugljikohidratima je jasan: da, ali **složeni**. Cilj je učiniti škrob što teže dostupnim tijelu kako bi probava odradila svoje. Zato preporučuje punozrnate i integralne namirnice, raznoliku prehranu, batat i krumpir, po mogućnosti s korom i ohlađen.

Objašnjava i mehanizam. Škrob ima razgranatu strukturu koju enzimi „opkole“ i s nje brzo odvajaju glukozu, pa ona brzo ulazi u krvotok. Kada se škrob „stisne“, enzimima je manje dostupan. To se postiže tako da se **tjestenina skuha al dente** ili da se **krumpir ohladi** i jede kao hladna krumpir-salata. Ana Pavlović dodaje da ga ne treba kombinirati s puno masnoće, a gošća se slaže. Rezultat je, kaže, posve drugačiji metabolički odgovor.

Tako savjetuje osobe s inzulinskom rezistencijom, one koji paze na hormonsku ravnotežu i one koji paze na težinu. Ističe da „nitko nema baš spor i brz metabolizam“. Važno je kolika je nečija potrošnja, kolike su potrebe i kakva je genetika.
sections.subtitle_en: Al dente pasta and cold potatoes: tricks with starch
sections.screenshot_description_en: Mirna Sentić explains how cooling potatoes and cooking al dente alter starch
sections.content_en:
Mirna's stance on carbohydrates is clear: yes, but **complex**. The goal is to make starch as difficult to access for the body as possible so that digestion does its work. Therefore, she recommends whole-grain and integral foods, a varied diet, sweet potato, and potato, preferably with the skin on and cooled.

She also explains the mechanism. Starch has a branched structure that enzymes "surround" and from which they quickly separate glucose, so it quickly enters the bloodstream. When starch is "compressed", it is less accessible to enzymes. This is achieved by **cooking pasta al dente** or by **cooling potatoes** and eating them as a cold potato salad. Ana Pavlović adds that it should not be combined with a lot of fat, and the guest agrees. The result, she says, is a completely different metabolic response.

This is how she advises people with insulin resistance, those who watch their hormonal balance, and those who watch their weight. She emphasizes that "no one has an entirely slow or fast metabolism". What is important is how much someone's expenditure is, what the needs are, and what the genetics are like.

sections.subtitle: Kad svjesnost postane kontrola: porast poremećaja hranjenja
sections.screenshot_description: Gošća upozorava da se i pretjerana kontrola u prehrani prenosi na djecu
sections.content:
Mirna Sentić primjećuje da se ljudi koji izbace gluten ili laktozu često osjećaju bolje jer su istodobno promijenili 80 posto svojih navika i počeli paziti na prehranu. Takva osoba djeluje vrlo svjesno. Gošća ipak upozorava da nije uvijek jasno je li riječ o pravoj svjesnosti ili je osoba skliznula u patologiju kontrole.

**„Ni kontrola nije dobra. Jer i ona se prenosi“**, kaže Mirna. Prenosi se na druge ljude, ali i na djecu. Poremećaji hranjenja stalno su u porastu. Gošća napominje da to nije njezino uže područje, ali da je gotovo svatko negdje na tom spektru. U njezinu su savjetovalištu sada dvije stručnjakinje, a kolegica **Sofija** specijalizirala se upravo za poremećaje hranjenja, uključujući liječenje anoreksije i bulimije.

Takve poremećaje opisuje kao život na rubu kontrole i opsesije. Uvijek su povezani s ranim uvjerenjima i odgojem. Hrana, zaključuje gošća, nije samo zadovoljavanje potreba. Ona je informacija koju tijelo prima i koja se u njemu zapisuje.
sections.subtitle_en: When awareness becomes control: the rise of eating disorders
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest warns that excessive control in nutrition is also passed on to children
sections.content_en:
Mirna Sentić observes that people who eliminate gluten or lactose often feel better because they simultaneously changed 80 percent of their habits and began paying attention to nutrition. Such a person appears very mindful. The guest nevertheless warns that it is not always clear whether this is true awareness or if the person has slipped into a pathology of control.

**"Control is not good either. Because it is passed on as well"**, says Mirna. It is passed on to other people, but also to children. Eating disorders are constantly on the rise. The guest notes that this is not her narrow field of expertise, but that almost everyone is somewhere on that spectrum. In her counseling center there are now two specialists, and her colleague **Sofija** specialized precisely in eating disorders, including the treatment of anorexia and bulimia.

She describes such disorders as living on the edge of control and obsession. They are always connected to early beliefs and upbringing. Food, concludes the guest, is not just satisfying needs. It is information that the body receives and that is recorded within it.

sections.subtitle: Cijelo voće umjesto soka i mimoza uz kajganu
sections.screenshot_description: Mirna Sentić objašnjava razliku između cijelog voća i cijeđenog soka
sections.content:
O voću Mirna Sentić govori bez straha: **fruktoza je „najnormalniji šećer“**. Ipak, uvijek preporučuje cijelo voće umjesto cijeđenog soka. Priroda je, kaže, voću dala vlakna i bolju strukturu, svoj „Mercedes“, pa jabuka ili banana dulje drže sitost od shakea od banane.

Objašnjava i zašto. Iz soka šećer brže ulazi u krvotok, inzulin naglo poraste, ali nema što dugo „izgarati i tinjati“, pa brzo padne. Taj pad znači glad i osjećaj kao da se ništa nije pojelo. Zato se sok, kao i kolač, „ljubi uz obrok“.

To ilustrira kroz smijeh pričom o **mimozi**, koktelu od soka naranče i šampanjca. Prijateljici je objasnila da se mimoza pije uz kajganu: sama izaziva glad, a uz jaje je „taman“. Ana Pavlović u šali dodaje da je najbolje pivo, a Mirna se prisjeća kako su ona i kolegica **Marina** komentirale da je „šest piva ekvivalent obroka“.

Na kraju se vraća ozbiljnom tonu. Svi se hranimo, kao što svi odgajamo djecu, ali malo tko poznaje načela i ima kritičan stav. Kada se zapne, potrebno je finije znanje: biokemija, iskustvo i sve što se s godinama skupi.
sections.subtitle_en: Whole fruit instead of juice and a mimosa with scrambled eggs
sections.screenshot_description_en: Mirna Sentić explains the difference between whole fruit and squeezed juice
sections.content_en:
About fruit Mirna Sentić speaks without fear: **fructose is "the most normal sugar"**. Still, she always recommends whole fruit instead of squeezed juice. Nature, she says, gave fruit fiber and a better structure, its "Mercedes", so an apple or a banana keeps satiety longer than a banana shake.

She also explains why. From juice, sugar enters the bloodstream faster, insulin rises sharply, but has nothing to "burn and smolder" for long, so it quickly drops. That drop means hunger and a feeling as if nothing was eaten. That is why juice, like cake, "kisses well with a meal".

She illustrates this with a laugh through the story of a **mimosa**, a cocktail made of orange juice and champagne. She explained to a friend that a mimosa is drunk with scrambled eggs: on its own it causes hunger, but with an egg it is "just right". Ana Pavlović jokingly adds that beer is the best, and Mirna recalls how she and her colleague **Marina** commented that "six beers is the equivalent of a meal".

In the end, she returns to a serious tone. We all eat, just as we all raise children, but few know the principles and have a critical stance. When one gets stuck, finer knowledge is needed: biochemistry, experience, and everything that accumulates over the years.

sections.subtitle: Prvo struka, pa umjetna inteligencija, a nastavak o nadutosti na Patreonu
sections.screenshot_description: Gošća savjetuje da se prije umjetne inteligencije pita struka, a voditeljica najavljuje nastavak
sections.content:
Mirna Sentić zaključuje dio razgovora za YouTube publiku porukom koja vrijedi od roditeljstva do prehrane: kada se izgubite, **pitajte struku prije nego umjetnu inteligenciju**. Umjetna inteligencija postoji i može pomoći, a Ana Pavlović dodaje da će često reći ono što korisnik želi čuti. Ipak, gošća je provjerava i priznaje da zna preporučiti i stručnjaka.

Ana Pavlović zahvaljuje Mirni i otkriva da razgovor zapravo nije gotov. Sljedeća tema je ona koja je, kako kaže, „zapalila“ njezin Instagram profil: **nadutost**. Pitanje „zašto ujutro imam ravan trbuh, a navečer izgledam kao u šestom mjesecu trudnoće?“ obradit će se u nastavku dostupnom na **Patreonu**. Voditeljica poziva gledatelje da se pretplate na podcast „Rastući s djecom“ i najavljuje novu epizodu za nekoliko tjedana.
sections.subtitle_en: Professionals first, then artificial intelligence, and the continuation about bloating on Patreon
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest advises asking professionals before artificial intelligence, and the host announces the continuation
sections.content_en:
Mirna Sentić concludes the portion of the conversation for the YouTube audience with a message that applies from parenting to nutrition: when you get lost, **ask the profession before artificial intelligence**. Artificial intelligence exists and can help, and Ana Pavlović adds that it will often say what the user wants to hear. Still, the guest tests it and admits that it also knows how to recommend a professional.

Ana Pavlović thanks Mirna and reveals that the conversation is actually not over. The next topic is the one that, as she says, "set fire" to her Instagram profile: **bloating**. The question "why do I have a flat stomach in the morning, and in the evening look like I'm in the sixth month of pregnancy?" will be addressed in the continuation available on **Patreon**. The host invites viewers to subscribe to the podcast "Rastući s djecom" and announces a new episode in a few weeks.
